articles.title: Eleições nos EUA 2026: acompanhe as últimas notícias sobre as midterms
articles.summary: Votação será em 3 de novembro e vai renovar a Câmara e um terço do Senado. Trump tenta manter a maioria republicana no Congresso.
articles.body:
Votação será em 3 de novembro e vai renovar a Câmara e um terço do Senado. Trump tenta manter a maioria republicana no Congresso.

Os americanos vão as urnas na próxima terça-feira (3) para renovar boa parte do Congresso e eleger governadores de 26 estados.

Chamadas de midterms , as eleições de meio de mandato de 2026 são cruciais para Trump e vão definir quanto poder ele terá no seus próximos 2 anos de mandato.

Projeções indicam que o Partido Democrata, que faz oposição a Donald Trump, pode conquistar o controle da Câmara e do Senado .

Após mínima histórica, aprovação de Trump sobe 1%

Após atingir a mínima histórica na semana passada, a aprovação de Donald Trump subiu 1% e foi para 32% , segundo pesquisa Reuters/Ipsos divulgada na segunda-feira (26).

Pesquisas divulgadas nos últimos dias, no entanto, apontam que a desaprovação do governo norte-americano está acima dos 60% .

Trump oferece US$ 1 milhão por denúncias de fraude eleitoral

A uma semana da eleição, Donald Trump anunciou que os EUA ofereceriam US$ 1 milhão a qualquer pessoa que denunciasse uma fraude eleitoral que resultasse em prisão e condenação.

O governo Trump tem adotado uma postura cada vez mais agressiva em relação à supervisão eleitoral, pressionando estados por dados de registro de eleitores. Especialistas políticos, autoridades eleitorais democratas e alguns republicanos veem essas ações como uma interferência indevida do governo federal.

Todas as 435 cadeiras da Câmara e cerca de um terço do Senado estão em disputa. Também há eleição para governador em 36 estados.

Daqui a exatamente uma semana, os americanos vão as urnas para eleger escolher deputados, senadores e 36 governadores. Está em jogo o controle do Congresso pelos próximos dois anos, e portanto quanto poder o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, terá no restante de seu mandato.

O g1 acompanha a reta final da campanha e traz as últimas notícias sobre a disputa. No dia da eleição, você pode acompanhar os resultados em tempo real.

articles.title: Acidente em São José dos Campos: carro bate em poste e invade imóvel | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente aconteceu na madrugada desta terça-feira (27), na Avenida Linneu de Moura, sentido Urbanova; trânsito foi bloqueado temporariamente e liberado às 4h30.
articles.summary: O acidente em São José dos Campos na Avenida Linneu de Moura bloqueou o trânsito após um carro bater em um poste e atingir o pátio de uma imobiliária.
articles.body:
Carro bate em poste, derruba fiação e cai em estacionamento de imobiliária em São José dos Campos — Foto: Andressa Lorenzetti/TV Vanguarda

Um carro bateu em um poste de iluminação na madrugada desta terça-feira (27), na Avenida Linneu de Moura, em São José dos Campos . Com o impacto, o veículo subiu na calçada e foi parar no estacionamento de uma imobiliária.

Segundo a Prefeitura de São José dos Campos, o acidente aconteceu próximo ao número 1.900 da avenida, no sentido Urbanova. Agentes de mobilidade urbana atenderam à ocorrência.

A fiação ficou sobre a pista, e o trânsito precisou ser bloqueado temporariamente. A via foi liberada às 4h30.

De acordo com a prefeitura, não houve vítimas. Uma equipe da Urbam trabalhava no local nesta manhã.

articles.title: Orçamento para 2027 será de R$ 27,9 bilhões em MS | G1
articles.standfirst: Projeto da Lei Orçamentária Anual (LOA) foi enviado à Assembleia Legislativa e prevê aumento de 2,95% em relação ao orçamento deste ano. Educação, Previdência e investimentos concentram parte significativa dos recursos. Proposta deve ser votada e aprovada até 22 de dezembro.
articles.summary: Projeto da Lei Orçamentária Anual (LOA) foi enviado à Assembleia Legislativa e prevê aumento de 2,95% em relação ao orçamento deste ano. Proposta deve ser votada e aprovada até 22
articles.body:
Plenário da Assembleia Legislativa de Mato Grosso do Sul. — Foto: ALEMS/Reprodução

O Governo de Mato Grosso do Sul enviou à Assembleia Legislativa de Mato Grosso do Sul (ALEMS) a proposta da Lei Orçamentária Anual (LOA) de 2027 com receita estimada em R$ 27,99 bilhões. O projeto foi recebido pelos deputados nesta segunda-feira (26) e estabelece a previsão de arrecadação e despesas do Estado para o primeiro ano do segundo mandato do governador Eduardo Riedel (PP).

O valor previsto representa crescimento de 2,95% em relação ao orçamento de 2026, estimado em R$ 27,19 bilhões. A proposta foi elaborada com base na Lei de Diretrizes Orçamentárias (LDO) aprovada neste ano, que define as metas e prioridades da administração estadual para 2027.

Segundo o projeto, a maior parte dos recursos deverá vir das receitas correntes, como arrecadação de impostos e transferências, estimadas em R$ 24,64 bilhões. Também estão previstos R$ 502,3 milhões em receitas de capital e R$ 2,84 bilhões em receitas intraorçamentárias.

Do lado das despesas, o Estado projeta gastar R$ 20,48 bilhões com despesas correntes, R$ 3,61 bilhões com despesas de capital e R$ 117,2 milhões na reserva de contingência, destinada a situações imprevistas.

Educação, Previdência e folha de pagamento lideram gastos

O detalhamento da proposta mostra que as despesas com pessoal e encargos sociais devem consumir R$ 13,49 bilhões em 2027. Os investimentos previstos somam R$ 2,45 bilhões.

Entre as áreas que concentram mais recursos estão a Previdência Social, com previsão de R$ 5,69 bilhões, e a Educação, que deverá receber R$ 4,64 bilhões. O projeto também reserva recursos para pagamento da dívida pública, precatórios e emendas parlamentares.

Contextualização: a LOA é a lei que define quanto o governo espera arrecadar e como os recursos serão distribuídos entre serviços públicos, investimentos e manutenção da máquina pública ao longo do ano.

A proposta também prevê os valores destinados aos demais Poderes e órgãos autônomos do Estado por meio dos duodécimos. Os repasses previstos são:

Assembleia Legislativa: R$ 567,5 milhões;

Tribunal de Contas do Estado: R$ 454 milhões;

Tribunal de Justiça de Mato Grosso do Sul: R$ 1,5 bilhão;

Ministério Público de Mato Grosso do Sul: R$ 812,3 milhões;

Defensoria Pública de Mato Grosso do Sul: R$ 377,3 milhões.

Esses órgãos devem encaminhar suas propostas orçamentárias ao órgão central de orçamento do Estado para consolidação do texto final, observando as regras da Lei de Responsabilidade Fiscal.

O projeto começará a ser analisado pela Comissão de Constituição, Justiça e Redação (CCJR) da Assembleia. Se receber parecer favorável, seguirá para votação em plenário e depois passará pela Comissão de Finanças e Orçamento antes da votação final pelos deputados estaduais.

A expectativa é que a proposta seja votada antes do recesso parlamentar, previsto para começar em 22 de dezembro.

articles.title: Ex-bispo é julgado por abuso sexual contra padre | G1
articles.standfirst: Sessão será realizada por videoconferência, às 13h30. Denúncia do Ministério Público aponta episódios entre 2019 e 2023 e pede a condenação de Valdir Mamede, ex-bispo de Catanduva (SP).
articles.summary: O ex-bispo Valdir Mamede é julgado nesta terça-feira por abusos sexuais contra um padre, em processo que apura crimes ocorridos entre 2019 e 2023 em Catanduva.
articles.body:
Bispo Dom Valdir Mamede renunciou ao cargo em Catanduva (SP) — Foto: Diocese de Catanduva/Divulgação

O ex-bispo de Catanduva (SP), Valdir Mamede, é julgado nesta terça-feira (27), às 13h30, após ser acusado de praticar uma série de abusos sexuais contra um padre entre 2019 e 2023 . A sessão será realizada por videoconferência.

A audiência é uma etapa do processo em que são produzidas provas, com depoimentos da vítima e das testemunhas, além do interrogatório do réu. Depois, a acusação e a defesa apresentam seus argumentos, e o juiz analisa as provas para decidir o caso.

A denúncia do Ministério Público aponta que os episódios teriam ocorrido entre 2019 e 2023, quando Dom Valdir exercia o comando da Diocese de Catanduva.

Segundo a acusação, ele teria se aproveitado da posição hierárquica e da autoridade religiosa sobre o padre para praticar atos libidinosos sem consentimento .

Valdir Mamede era bispo auxiliar da Arquidiocese de Brasília e assumiu o Bispado de Catanduva. Os fatos teriam acontecido na Residência Episcopal e na Paróquia de São Sebastião, em Ibirá (SP), onde o padre atuava.

Em manifestação anterior, Valdir afirmou que sempre agiu de forma ética e que os episódios foram consensuais. O g1 tenta contato novamente com a defesa do acusado.

Conversas por app mostram que ex-bispo de Catanduva (SP) pediu para padre que denunciou estupro 'passar a máquina' para depilar corpo — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

O boletim de ocorrência foi registrado pelo padre no dia 22 de março de 2024. De acordo com a denúncia do MP, emitida em abril deste ano, a aproximação entre eles começou sob o pretexto de que o então bispo precisava de cuidados pessoais, incluindo depilação corporal íntima.

Segundo o documento, os abusos teriam ocorrido de forma reiterada durante cerca de cinco anos. O MP descreve quatro episódios considerados criminosos, entre eles:

Relação de hierarquia: a Promotoria afirma que o ex-bispo teria usado a relação de autoridade e a vulnerabilidade psicológica do padre para constrangê-lo, com ameaças veladas de punições religiosas, como transferência de paróquia ou impedimento do exercício do sacerdócio;

Depilação : o ex-bispo pediu para que a vítima depilasse o corpo dele e passasse, mais de uma vez, a máquina de barbear no corpo como pretexto para ficar nu e cometer o assédio sexual. Em 2024, o g1 divulgou pela primeira vez os prints de conversas por aplicativo que mostram que o ex-bispo pediu para que a vítima depilasse o corpo dele ;

Ligações de vídeo: o ex-bispo fazia chamadas de vídeo em que teria se exibido nu e se masturbado diante do padre;

Violência sexual: em um deles, em setembro de 2022, o então bispo teria chamado o padre para dormir na Residência Episcopal, em Catanduva, antes de uma viagem no dia seguinte. Segundo a acusação, durante a noite, Valdir teria agarrado o religioso e praticado atos sexuais sem o consentimento dele. Em outro episódio, em 2023, Valdir teria ido à casa do religioso, em Ibirá, tentado agarrá-lo e se masturbado ao lado dele sem consentimento.

Ainda conforme a denúncia, após o último episódio, a vítima recolheu material biológico deixado em um lençol e o encaminhou para análise. O laudo pericial citado pelo MP apontou que o material era proveniente de um indivíduo do sexo masculino.

O Ministério Público pede a condenação de Valdir por importunação sexual praticada reiteradamente, com agravantes relacionados às circunstâncias dos fatos e ao exercício de autoridade sobre a vítima.

A Promotoria também solicita o pagamento de indenização mínima de R$ 300 mil por danos morais. Devido às pressões e danos psicológicos, o padre está de licença médica e afastado dos trabalhos na Igreja.

Ex-bispo renunciou ao cargo na Diocese de Catanduva (SP) — Foto: Divulgação

A denúncia foi apresentada pelo Ministério Público em 28 de abril e recebida pela Justiça em 30 de junho de 2026. Com a decisão, Valdir passou à condição de réu . O processo tramita sob segredo de Justiça na 2ª Vara Criminal de Catanduva.

O ex-bispo chegou a renunciar ao cargo, em novembro de 2023, sem apresentar o motivo.

articles.title: Camila Kfouri, filha do jornalista Juca Kfouri, morre aos 48 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Psicóloga e psicanalista, Camila foi fundadora da Clínica da Cidade e também atuou como DJ. Amiga há 31 anos, a artista plástica Rita Wainer lamentou a morte nas redes sociais.
articles.summary: Psicóloga e psicanalista, Camila foi fundadora da Clínica da Cidade e também atuou como DJ. Amiga há 31 anos, a artista plástica Rita Wainer lamentou a morte nas redes sociais.
articles.body:
Camila Kfouri, filha do jornalista Juca Kfouri, morreu nesta segunda-feira (26), aos 48 anos. A morte foi anunciada pelo pai em um texto publicado no UOL. A causa não havia sido divulgada até a publicação desta reportagem.

Psicóloga e psicanalista, Camila foi uma das fundadoras da Clínica da Cidade e integrou o Laboratório de Estudos da Violência e Vulnerabilidade Social da Universidade Mackenzie, além da Clínica Pública de Psicanálise.

Em sua despedida, Juca Kfouri relembrou a trajetória da filha e expressou a dor da perda. O jornalista contou que Camila enfrentou problemas de saúde ao longo da vida, após presenciar, aos seis anos, o avô paterno ser baleado durante um assalto na porta de casa.

“Só sei que a levarei comigo até o fim”, escreveu o jornalista.

A artista plástica Rita Wainer, amiga de Camila há 31 anos, também lamentou a morte em uma publicação no Instagram. No texto, ela contou que recebeu a notícia por meio de uma ligação às 19h15 e descreveu a dificuldade de assimilar a perda.

“São 31 anos de amizade. Você sabia tudo que eu fazia, falava e pensava”, escreveu Rita.

A artista contou que, desde que soube da morte, não conseguia encontrar palavras para expressar o que estava sentindo. “Eu queria escrever palavras bonitas e desde as 7:15 meu coração tá off-line”, afirmou.

Na homenagem, a artista mencionou familiares, amigos e pacientes de Camila e questionou como todos enfrentariam a perda.

O velório de Camila Kfouri será realizado nesta terça-feira (27), das 11h às 15h, no Cerimonial Pacaembu, na Avenida Pacaembu, 1254, no bairro do Pacaembu, na Zona Oeste de São Paulo. Após a despedida, haverá uma cerimônia de cremação, marcada para as 16h30, no Crematório Vila Alpina, na Avenida Francisco Falconi, 437, na Zona Leste da capital.

articles.summary: Atendimentos ocorrerão em 3 unidades da Fundação Hospitalar municipal. Para agendar, é preciso apresentar documento com foto, cartão do SUS e comprovante de residência.
articles.body:
Consulta homem paciente — Foto: Reprodução/pressfoto/Freepik

Uma campanha do Novembro Azul vai disponibilizar 5 mil vagas para consultas e exames gratuitos em Feira de Santana , segunda maior cidade da Bahia. Os agendamentos começam em 3 de novembro e são destinados exclusivamente a pessoas que moram no município.

Os atendimentos serão realizados presencialmente em três unidades da Fundação Hospitalar de Feira de Santana: o Centro Municipal de Diagnóstico por Imagem (CMDI), no bairro Baraúnas; outra unidade do CMDI, na Avenida Maria Quitéria; e o Centro Municipal de Prevenção ao Câncer (CMPC), no centro da cidade.

Além de consultas com urologistas, a campanha vai oferecer os seguintes serviços:

Além dos atendimentos nas unidades, serão realizados dois mutirões para oferecer parte dos serviços. O primeiro será no dia 7 de novembro, com atendimentos de raio-X, ECG, ultrassonografias, nutricionista, clínico geral e cardiologista.

O segundo mutirão será realizado em 14 de novembro e contará com serviços de raio-X, ECG, ultrassonografias, psicólogo, clínico geral, angiologista e nutricionista.

Os atendimentos nos dois dias são limitados à quantidade de vagas disponíveis. Durante os mutirões, também serão realizadas marcações para consultas em outras datas nas especialidades de:

Para ter acesso aos serviços, os interessados devem apresentar documento oficial de identificação com foto, cartão do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) e comprovante de residência. A campanha é destinada a homens de qualquer idade.

Segundo a presidente da Fundação Hospitalar, Gilberte Lucas, embora a procura seja maior entre homens a partir dos 40 anos, pessoas mais jovens também devem ficar atentas aos cuidados com a saúde.

A campanha Novembro Azul tem como objetivo incentivar os cuidados com a saúde masculina e a prevenção do câncer de próstata.

articles.title: Mega-Sena: dois bolões do Ceará acertam quina e levam até R$ 194 mil | G1
articles.standfirst: Os dois bilhetes foram bolões, com valores que serão divididos entre dezenas de apostadores. Ninguém acertou os seis números, e a Mega acumulou em R$ 305 milhões.
articles.summary: Os dois bilhetes foram bolões, com valores que serão divididos entre dezenas de apostadores. Ninguém acertou os seis números, e a Mega acumulou em R$ 305 milhões.
articles.body:
Volante da Mega-Sena — Foto: Ana Marin/g1

Duas apostas feitas no Ceará acertaram cinco números sorteados da Mega-Sena nesta segunda-feira (26) e levaram prêmios de até R$ 194 mil. Os bilhetes foram bolões com dezenas de participantes. Ninguém acertou os seis números, e a Mega acumulou em R$ 305 milhões com sorteio nesta terça-feira (27).

Veja os números sorteados: 07 - 10 - 14 - 27 - 36 - 55

As duas apostas foram feitas nas cidades de Fortaleza e Iguatu . O bolão de Fortaleza fez uma aposta de 15 números, que custa a partir de R$ 30.030,00 . Foram 100 apostadores no bolão realizado pela Loteria Aldeota. Isto significa que cada apostador investiu cerca de R$ 300,30.

Ao acertar cinco números, o bolão feito em Fortaleza levou o prêmio de R$ 194.331,00. Após a divisão do prêmio, cada apostador deve receber R$ 1.943,00.

Nesta segunda-feira (26), os apostadores que acertaram cinco números em jogos simples levaram o prêmio de R$19.433,12.

Veja os valores para quem acertou a quina e a quadra:

5 acertos: 182 apostas ganhadoras, R$ 19.433,12

4 acertos: 11.018 apostas ganhadoras, R$ 458,57

No entanto, os prêmios são multiplicados para quem faz apostas mais altas, com mais números escolhidos.

Em Iguatu, o bolão que acertou a quina da Mega apostou 10 números e teve 31 cotas . A aposta de bolão com esta quantidade de números custa R$ 1.260,00, e cada apostador investiu um valor de aproximadamente R$ 40. O prêmio conquistado foi de R$ 97.165,47. Após a divisão, cada um deve ficar com R$ 3.134,37.

Esta semana é a Mega Semana, que terá cinco sorteios consecutivos até sexta-feira (30) . O g1 transmite ao vivo o sorteio desta terça-feira (27) , com prêmio acumulado em R$ 305 milhões.

As apostas podem ser realizadas até as 20h (horário de Brasília) em qualquer lotérica do país ou por meio do site e aplicativo Loterias Caixa, disponíveis em smartphones, computadores e outros dispositivos.

Já os bolões digitais poderão ser comprados até as 20h30, exclusivamente pelo portal Loterias Online e pelo aplicativo.

Ainda segundo a Caixa, para os sorteios realizados aos domingos as apostas simples podem ser efetuadas até às 22h de sábado por meio das unidades lotéricas, pelo Portal Loterias Caixa e do aplicativo Loterias Caixa.

A comercialização dos Bolões Caixa nos canais eletrônicos, nesse caso, acontece até às 10h45 do domingo, quinze minutos antes da realização dos sorteios.

O pagamento da aposta online pode ser realizado via PIX, cartão de crédito ou pelo internet banking, para correntistas da Caixa. É preciso ter 18 anos ou mais para participar.

A probabilidade de vencer em cada concurso varia de acordo com o número de dezenas jogadas e do tipo de aposta realizada. Para um jogo simples, com apenas seis dezenas, que custa R$ 6, a probabilidade de ganhar o prêmio milionário é de 1 em 50.063.860, segundo a Caixa.

Já para uma aposta com 20 dezenas (limite máximo), com o preço de R$ 232.560,00, a probabilidade de acertar o prêmio é de 1 em 1.292, ainda de acordo com a instituição.

articles.title: Justiça suspende corte de árvores em campo de golfe que Trump quer reformar em Washington | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente americano pretende transformar espaço público em instalação capaz de receber grandes torneios; ambientalistas questionam as obras.
articles.summary: Presidente americano pretende transformar espaço público em instalação capaz de receber grandes torneios; ambientalistas questionam as obras.
articles.body:
As obras no Salão de Baile da Casa Branca (R) são vistas do topo do Monumento a Washington, em Washington, D.C., no dia 22 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Foto por SAUL LOEB / AFP

Uma juíza federal dos Estados Unidos suspendeu, na segunda-feira (26), até nova ordem, o corte de árvores no campo de golfe East Potomac Golf Links, em Washington. A decisão interrompe parte das obras de renovação do espaço, um dos projetos impulsionados pelo presidente Donald Trump na capital americana.

Centenas de árvores já haviam sido cortadas no local, que é público e conhecido pelas tarifas acessíveis. Trump, que é um praticante frequente de golfe e dono de campos em diferentes países, pretende transformar o espaço em uma instalação capaz de receber grandes torneios.

As obras começaram apesar de uma ação judicial movida por um grupo ambientalista e da oposição de golfistas locais. Eles argumentam que o campo, com cerca de 100 anos de história, é um dos poucos espaços da região onde é possível praticar o esporte a preços acessíveis.

Na decisão, a juíza Ana Reyes determinou que o governo não pode derrubar ou danificar novas árvores no campo. A ordem também exige que as autoridades emitam um aviso por escrito com pelo menos 10 dias úteis de antecedência antes de realizar qualquer alteração irreversível no local.

Reyes já havia determinado uma suspensão temporária dos trabalhos. Com a nova decisão, voltou a dar razão aos defensores do meio ambiente.

Em 10 de outubro, ativistas manifestaram preocupação com o corte de quase 500 árvores no campo de golfe e com os planos das autoridades de derrubar centenas de outras.

articles.title: 2 weeks, 2 Keralam teen drivers, 2 luxury cars, 4 deaths: How parents can be held liable when minors take the wheel

articles.body: KOCHI: In two weeks, two reckless teen drivers pushed four families into grief.The two cases put not only the accused but also their parents in the dock, legally and morally.Legal experts said parents, who allow their children to drive, can’t claim ignorance of a minor taking a vehicle to evade legal repercussions.Under Motor Vehicles Act, the burden is on the parents to prove what precautions they took to prevent it, they said.Retired HC judge B Kemal Pasha said the father of the teenager who rammed a luxury sedan and killed a 55-year-old scooter rider cannot defend himself by claiming that his son had taken the vehicle without his knowledge.The fact that the teen clocked over 100km/hr indicates that he had probably driven before, which can strengthen the father’s culpability, said Pasha.“If he is driving above 100, then it is not his first time. He must have practised and I don’t think this was an isolated incident and he (dad) cannot say that he was unaware,” said Pasha, adding that it is surprising that the father is a judge, who is aware of the law.Since the father is the registered owner, it was his responsibility to keep the car keys safe.Even if he says that his son took the vehicle without his knowledge, it would mean he created the circumstances for him to do so.MV Act clearly places the burden on the vehicle owner or guardian to prove that the offence was committed without his knowledge or that he had exercised due diligence to prevent it.That means he needs to prove that it was done without his knowledge. It is not easy, said Pasha.He said the action taken in the case should send a strong message to parents about allowing minors to drive.The accident at Nedumbassery also had an element of parental involvement. After the accident, the accused teen reportedly told people that his father would take care of the case.Senior consultant psychiatrist at Medical Trust Hospital Dr CJ John said boys have a fascination for vehicles.“They instinctively want to drive if there is a vehicle at home. There is a section of parents who succumb to their demands or even boast about it before others instead of firmly telling their children that it is illegal. articles.title: Kuno cheetah cub dies after suspected shooting outside protected area, first such case since 2022 reintroduction
articles.summary: BHOPAL: A 19-month-old male cheetah cub at Kuno National Park, which was found with multiple pellets lodged in its abdomen after a suspected close-range
articles.body: BHOPAL: A 19-month-old male cheetah cub at Kuno National Park, which was found with multiple pellets lodged in its abdomen after a suspected close-range shooting, has died, forest department sources said.The cub, one of Nirva’s offspring, had been shifted to a medical facility in Jabalpur for advanced treatment after being rescued from a forest area bordering Sheopur and Morena districts on the night of October 25.The death is a major setback for Project Cheetah and raises concerns over the safety of the big cats outside the protected park area.It would be the first reported suspected shooting of a cheetah since the species was reintroduced in India in September 2022.Three or four metal pellets had been detected inside the cub’s abdominal cavity. Investigators are examining the nature of the weapon used and the circumstances in which the animal was shot.The Special Tiger Strike Force (STSF), a specialised wildlife protection unit, has been deployed in the area. The forest department is also seeking assistance from the state police’s Special Task Force to identify those responsible, officials said.The cub was found injured by a monitoring team on the evening of October 25 while ranging in the territorial forest division of Morena, bordering Sheopur district.It was rescued overnight and brought to Kuno for initial medical examination before being shifted to Jabalpur for further treatment.Morena is known for its ravine-dotted terrain and the widespread availability of country-made firearms in some pockets.Investigators are exploring whether the animal was shot with a traditional bharmar, a muzzle-loading firearm, or a country-made 12-bore gun. A forensic and ballistic examination is expected to help establish the type of weapon used.Some officials suspect the shooter may have fired in panic after encountering the young cheetah in the forest, possibly mistaking it for a leopard.However, the motive and circumstances remain unconfirmed, and no suspect has been identified.In a statement, Kuno authorities said an investigation was under way to determine the cause of the injuries and that all possible angles were being examined.The statement, issued by the Additional Principal Chief Conservator of Forests and Field Director of the Cheetah Project, did not explicitly mention a shooting.State chief wildlife warden Samita Rajora had earlier said the case was being investigated from all angles and that it was too early to comment on the cause of the injuries.The incident has renewed concerns about the threats cheetahs face while moving beyond protected areas. The first action plan for Project Cheetah had flagged the prevalence of bushmeat consumption and the possession of country-made firearms, bows, arrows and other hunting tools in the region.Poaching has been a persistent concern in the landscape around Kuno. In April 2022, months before the first cheetahs arrived from Namibia, a leopard was killed by poachers in the park’s buffer zone.Deer poaching has also been reported in surrounding areas, while forest officials have previously suspected hunting groups of entering protected areas and removing camera traps to avoid detection.Cheetahs were declared extinct in India in 1952. Their return is the centrepiece of Project Cheetah, launched in 2022, under which animals were brought from Africa to Kuno as part of a programme to re-establish the species in the country.Wildlife activist Ajay Dubey has demanded a CBI inquiry into the matter following interstate ramification.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bhopal | Silver Rate in Bhopal | Bank Holidays in Bhopal | Public Holidays in Bhopal | Petrol Price in Bhopal | Diesel Price in Bhopal | CNG Price in Bhopal | LPG Price in BhopalStay updated with the latest Bhopal news. articles.title: Dyson study finds 1 in 2 Indians frequently miss cleaning under beds and furniture
articles.summary: More than half of Indian households are missing hard-to-reach areas such as spaces under beds and furniture during routine cleaning, according to Dyson's
articles.body: More than half of Indian households are missing hard-to-reach areas such as spaces under beds and furniture during routine cleaning, according to Dyson's first 'How India Cleans' study. The survey also found that hair left behind on floors and dust quickly resettling after cleaning remain among the biggest frustrations for consumers. The study, conducted among over 650 respondents across seven Indian cities, examines how Indians clean their homes, the challenges they face and what they expect from modern floorcare technology. According to the findings, 52% of respondents said spaces beneath beds and furniture are frequently missed during cleaning, while 48% reported difficulties cleaning corners, edges and skirting areas.Despite significant time spent on household cleaning, many consumers continue to struggle with achieving a thorough clean. Dyson said more than half of respondents spend between 30 minutes and an hour cleaning floors, while another 11% spend up to two hours.The study highlights that the issue is not just how often people clean, but whether existing cleaning tools can effectively tackle different surfaces and hard-to-reach spaces throughout the home.According to the survey, 36% of respondents identified human or pet hair left behind on floors as one of their biggest cleaning pain points. Meanwhile, 38% said dust settles again quickly after cleaning, creating the impression that surfaces become dirty soon after they have been cleaned. Dyson noted that household dust can easily become airborne due to everyday activity before resettling on surfaces, making effective dust removal a continuing challenge.The study found that Indian households often feature a mix of flooring types that require different cleaning approaches. While hard flooring remains common, 72% of respondents said they also have carpets and rugs at home. Other common surfaces include marble (51%), vitrified or ceramic tiles (49%), and granite (43%). This diversity means consumers increasingly seek cleaning solutions that can move seamlessly across different floor types without compromising performance.When selecting floorcare products, respondents indicated a strong preference for advanced technology. Around 61% said better technology influenced their purchase decisions, ahead of cleaning performance (54%) and brand trust (49%). In comparison, only 21% cited pricing and promotional offers as a key factor. The survey also found that vacuum cleaners are increasingly being used for whole-home cleaning rather than just floor maintenance. Respondents reported using them under furniture (71%), on hard floors (70%), carpets and rugs (69%), upholstery (69%), and beds and mattresses (63%).Commenting on the findings, Tim Hare, Design and Development Engineer, Floor Care at Dyson, said consumers increasingly expect vacuum cleaners to tackle multiple cleaning challenges in a single session, ranging from fine dust and long hair to different floor surfaces and hard-to-reach areas. The company said insights from the study help shape the development of future floorcare products by identifying real-world cleaning problems and unmet consumer needs.Alongside the study, Dyson highlighted its recently launched Dyson V16 Piston Animal cordless vacuum cleaner, priced at ₹79,900. The company said the device is designed to address common household cleaning challenges through features such as automatic floor-type sensing, anti-tangle technology for long hair, LED illumination for spotting hidden dust, and up to 70 minutes of fade-free suction.The appliance also includes Dyson's CleanCompaktor bin technology, which the company claims can compress dust and debris to increase storage capacity and reduce the frequency of emptying. The findings underscore a growing consumer focus on cleaning effectiveness rather than just effort, with many households seeking technology-driven solutions that can deliver a more complete clean across modern homes.You use AI every day. articles.title: Disturbing video shows days-old baby monkeys tormented in experiments at the University of Washington; the six-year study, costing $4.2 million, involved 32 pregnant macaques and 28 separated infants; Peta calls for the closure of US primate research centres
articles.summary: Newly released footage by the animal rights group Peta shows infant macaques, some only two days old, separated from their mothers and subjected to
articles.body: Newly released footage by the animal rights group Peta shows infant macaques, some only two days old, separated from their mothers and subjected to neurological tests at the University of Washington’s National Primate Research Center (WaNPRC). The video offers the first filmed look inside these experiments. It shows tiny monkeys shrieking in fear and gripping blankets, their only form of comfort, as researchers shave their heads, attach electrodes and test their reflexes and memory to determine whether exposure to a neurotoxin in the womb has damaged their developing brains. Peta obtained the video through a records request in September 2026. It was filmed between 2017 and 2019.Days-old baby monkeys separated from their mothers and killed after the experimentNewborn monkeys were separated from their mothers as part of an experiment investigating domoic acid, a neurotoxin produced by marine algae that accumulates in shellfish and can cause illness in humans. Researchers tested whether exposure to the toxin before birth damaged the infants’ brains. To do this, they dosed 32 pregnant macaques every day. After birth, 28 infants were taken from their mothers, bottle-fed, kept in incubators and later housed alone from the age of three weeks.In the heart-breaking video, the baby monkeys are seen sucking their fingers, screeching and jerking as scientists shave their heads and check their reflexes and memory.Dr Lisa Jones-Engel, Peta’s chief science adviser on primate issues, described the distressing conditions the infant monkeys endured during the experiments. “These monkeys are so young they still have the distinctive black fur of newborn macaques, yet instead of clinging to their mothers, they grasp blankets on metal tables,” the adviser told The Guardian. Jones-Engel spent 17 years as a primate scientist at the university before becoming one of its most outspoken critics. She has spent 35 years working as a primatologist.The project ran from 2014 to 2020 and received more than $4.2 million in funding from the National Institutes of Health (NIH). Some experiments lasted years. Peta says the monkeys were killed once the work ended. The research programme has operated at the university’s infant primate lab since 1971.Macaques are social animals that live in groups in the wild. Maternal care is essential for their social and behavioural development, Dr Malene Hansen, a long-tailed macaque expert, told the publication.Responding to concerns over the treatment of the infant monkeys, the Washington National Primate Research Center told The Guardian: “We recognise that research involving infant animals raises important questions about their wellbeing. Maternal relationships and early social development are important considerations in nonhuman primate welfare. Our experienced veterinary and animal care personnel have specialised expertise in primate care, including nursery rearing.”The NIH said it places a high priority on laboratory animal welfare. “All animals used in NIH-supported research are protected by laws, regulations and policies designed to ensure the smallest possible number of animals are used and their welfare is prioritised.”The WaNPRC said it is not currently conducting studies involving infant monkeys, although approved protocols for such research remain active.Unethical experiments Infant monkeys cannot thrive without their mothers, making separation itself unethical. “It is unethical to conduct research that separates infant macaques from their mothers. Period,” Hansen added.Jones-Engel makes a similar point about the reasoning behind the work. “There is no moral escape hatch. You can’t claim primates are used because they’re so like us, then take an infant away from its mother and experiment on it. You would never do that to a human primate. The cruelty also has biological consequences: maternal separation alters an infant’s physiology, immunity, behaviour and development, distorting its response to the very substance or disease being studied.” Jones-Engel’s transition from animal researcher to campaigner is documented in the new film Sentient.Jarrod Bailey, a research scientist, argues that biological differences often mean monkey experiments fail to produce treatments for human diseases, including HIV/AIDS, Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s. “We pay the price in failed treatments; monkeys pay with their lives. A shift away from monkey experiments would benefit all primates, including humans.”This footage offers a rare glimpse into experiments involving monkeys. Jones-Engel added: “For decades, the term ‘primate research’ has obscured the reality inside laboratories. These videos expose the suffering and raise a fundamental question: why are these facilities still operating at all?”The university says it is working to replace, reduce and refine animal experiments, although it maintains that “animal studies remain necessary for some complex scientific questions”. Peta is calling for the closure of all seven US National Primate Research Centers. “This is the same facility where Beth Buffalo deprives elderly monkeys of food and water to compel them to stare at a computer screen for up to nine hours in exchange for drops of juice, claiming this allows her to understand how the brain ages,” Peta said. The animal rights group has urged the public to share its video on social media and take action to help shut down the Washington National Primate Research Center.In the US, federal agencies are moving towards alternatives to reduce animal testing, including new approach methodologies such as organ-on-a-chip technology and computer modelling. Even so, more than 106,000 monkeys were held in US facilities in 2025, up 1.5 per cent from 2024. Between 2025 and 2026, more than 32,000 primates were imported from Asia and Africa for laboratory use, the publication said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2020, Alessia Cara pledged her share of royalties from a live EP to Save the Children for 21 years; a pandemic-era music release became a long-term commitment to vulnerable children
articles.summary: In the summer of 2020, Alessia Cara was preparing to release a live recording of music she had put out the previous year.
articles.body: In the summer of 2020, Alessia Cara was preparing to release a live recording of music she had put out the previous year. The project, This summer: live off the floor, had been planned before the coronavirus pandemic disrupted daily life across the world. By the time it was ready to reach listeners, however, Cara had decided to give the proceeds from the release a different purpose. The Canadian singer announced that she would donate her share of royalties from the EP to Save the Children for 21 years, as reported by Save the Children Canada. The commitment linked a single music project to a much longer period of support for children facing poverty, displacement and limited access to basic services.Alessia Cara pledged 21 years of EP royalties to support children worldwideCara announced the donation on 25 June 2020, explaining that the decision had followed the upheaval caused by the pandemic. She had released an EP the previous September and subsequently recorded a live version, which was scheduled to arrive in the summer of 2020. Rather than treating the release as a conventional music project, she chose to direct her proceeds towards the international children's charity over the following 21 years.The pledge concerned Cara's share of the royalties, rather than an announced fixed sum. No total donation amount was specified in the announcement, leaving the eventual value dependent on the income generated by the recordings over time. Its duration was a defining part of the arrangement: revenue from the EP could continue supporting the charity well beyond its initial release period.For an artist, royalties can provide income long after a recording first becomes available. In Cara's case, that continuing stream was intended to serve a charitable purpose, turning the release into a source of support that extended across decades.Save the Children donation targeted children in more than 100 countriesSave the Children works with children and families in countries affected by conflict, poverty, emergencies and other forms of hardship. Its programmes cover areas such as healthcare, nutrition, education, shelter and protection from violence and exploitation.President and CEO, Save the Children Bill Chambers said, “This incredible support will provide much-needed funds to advance the rights of children in Canada, Yemen and over 100 countries around the world. Through this partnership we will help the most marginalized and deprived children in crisis have the opportunity to survive, learn and be protected from harm, no matter who they are or where they’re from.”The disruption had reached well beyond hospitals and public health services. School closures left hundreds of millions of children without their usual classroom routines, while lost earnings placed additional pressure on families already struggling to afford food and other necessities. For children living in unstable circumstances, interruptions to education and access to care could compound problems that had existed long before the outbreak.Save the Children said the donation would help it extend its work with children who were particularly vulnerable to these pressures. The commitment was intended to support both immediate needs and its continuing programmes in the years that followed.Children in Yemen and Canada were among the groups highlightedCara specifically referred to children in Yemen, where years of conflict had left large numbers of young people facing severe humanitarian difficulties. In her announcement as reported by Save the Children Canada, she cited 12 million children experiencing hardship there. The figure reflected the scale of the crisis she wanted the donation to address, rather than a claim that the EP's proceeds would be allocated exclusively to the country.She also drew attention to Indigenous children in Canada and children of colour living in vulnerable communities. By naming these groups alongside children in Yemen, Cara described a commitment that crossed national boundaries and included children experiencing different forms of disadvantage.The reference to Canada was significant because the singer's charitable focus was not limited to emergencies overseas. Children can face barriers to education, healthcare, safety and other essential resources within wealthier countries, too. Cara's stated intention was to support Save the Children's work wherever assistance was needed across its international operations.The organisation's announcement also emphasised the importance of reaching children who were often hardest to support during periods of crisis. Its work included helping families meet immediate needs while protecting children's access to services that affect their longer-term development.Pandemic delays shaped Alessia Cara’s 21-year royalty pledgeWhen Cara explained her decision, she described the EP as a project that had been planned before the pandemic changed the circumstances surrounding its release. The original recording had come out in September 2019, with the live version following the next summer. By June 2020, the pandemic had altered how people worked, studied and maintained contact with one another, while placing additional demands on charities.Cara said the situation had reinforced her concern about children who lacked the resources needed to learn, remain safe and pursue opportunities. Her announcement connected those concerns to the practical support provided by Save the Children, including food, shelter, healthcare and education.The pledge also reflected the particular nature of the music industry. A recording can remain commercially available long after the publicity surrounding its launch has ended, producing royalties at different points in its life. By committing her share of those proceeds for 21 years, Cara attached a long-term charitable purpose to a release associated with a specific moment in 2020.There was no announced estimate of how much the EP would ultimately generate for the charity. The commitment was defined by the length of time over which the royalties would be donated, rather than by a publicly stated financial target.Save the Children welcomed Cara’s long-term support for children’s rightsIn its response, Save the Children welcomed the donation and said it would contribute to efforts to protect children's rights and improve their access to essential services. The organisation's then-president and chief executive, Bill Chambers, highlighted the continuing effects of the pandemic on families, including the loss of household income, interrupted schooling and concerns about children's wellbeing.The 21-year period gave the commitment a scope that went beyond the immediate emergency. While the pandemic had prompted Cara's decision, the charity's work also addressed longstanding challenges affecting children in communities around the world. Future royalties could therefore contribute to programmes operating under circumstances different from those that existed when the EP was released.Cara thanked the musicians who had worked on the recording and her team for supporting the decision. Her announcement did not set out a detailed distribution schedule or identify specific projects that would receive the proceeds.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: An Oklahoma man allegedly claimed he inherited a $5.4 million mansion, tried three times to record a deed and had electricity moved into his name; county clerks refused the filings and he now faces two felony charges
articles.summary: An Oklahoma man allegedly tried to claim ownership of a $5.4 million mansion by insisting he had inherited it from deceased relatives, but county clerks
articles.body: An Oklahoma man allegedly tried to claim ownership of a $5.4 million mansion by insisting he had inherited it from deceased relatives, but county clerks refused to record the paperwork he repeatedly submitted. According to the Oklahoma County Sheriff’s Office, 29-year-old Antonio Moore attempted three times to file a deed for the roughly 14,000-square-foot property in Oklahoma City’s gated Gaillardia neighborhood. The situation escalated after the legitimate homeowner discovered that electricity service had been moved into Moore’s name and that a bank had flagged an attempted loan using the mansion as collateral. Moore was arrested on September 30 and now faces two felony charges, including first-degree forgery and obtaining property by deception. The allegations remain unproven in court, and he is presumed innocent unless convicted. The case, first reported by Wealth of Geeks and local Oklahoma outlets, highlights how property-title fraud can begin with paperwork that looks official but fails basic verification. Read more details about it here:What investigators say happenedThe first reported incident occurred in April, when the homeowner’s association contacted the property owner after a man tried to enter the gated community and claimed the mansion had belonged to relatives who had died. Community security did not allow him inside, according to a sheriff’s report cited by KFOR. The man reportedly attempted to enter Gaillardia twice more during that same month. Sheriff Tommie Johnson III later publicly described the investigation on October 22, identifying the residence as a large home in the exclusive neighborhood. These early encounters became important because they reportedly preceded the more formal attempt to establish ownership through county records.The homeowner then began receiving correspondence addressed to Moore at the mansion, which raised further concerns. He also learned that electricity service had been transferred into Moore’s name, an unusual development for a property he still owned. According to the sheriff’s office, Bank of Oklahoma notified the homeowner about an attempted loan that used the residence as collateral. Johnson told KOCO that he believed Moore’s intended objective was to borrow money against the property. In other words, investigators allege that the claimed inheritance may have been part of an effort to make the mansion appear available for financing.Three refused deed filingsOn September 11, employees at the Oklahoma County Clerk’s Office alerted sheriff’s deputies after receiving paperwork that purported to show Moore had inherited the mansion, as per reports. The legitimate homeowner also went to the office to report possible fraud. Clerk’s office staff reviewed the documents carefully, explained why they could not be recorded, and asked additional questions, according to information reported by FOX 25. Despite that refusal, investigators said Moore returned to the office twice more with similar paperwork. The repeated filings ultimately became central evidence in the case described by the sheriff’s office.A deed does not automatically create lawful ownership simply because someone prepares or presents it. County recording offices generally assess whether documents meet filing requirements, but they do not adjudicate every underlying ownership dispute. In this instance, employees declined to record the disputed deed, preventing it from entering the official land records. Sheriff Johnson warned that even if an unauthorized document is recorded, it can complicate later title searches and property transactions. Clearing such a record may require legal proceedings, which is why early detection matters for homeowners.The felony chargesOklahoma County court records identify the defendant as Antonio D Shay Moore and show that prosecutors filed two felony counts on September 30. The first count is first-degree forgery under Oklahoma law, while the second alleges obtaining property by trick, deception, or false representation. The court docket for State of Oklahoma v. Antonio D Shay Moore, case CF-2026-5325, records an initial appearance on October 6. A judge set bail at $25,000 and tentatively appointed a public defender. A preliminary-hearing conference was scheduled for October 27 at 9 a.m, reported Wealth of Geeks.It is important to distinguish an allegation from a conviction. Moore has not been found guilty, and the charges will need to be proven through the normal legal process. The sheriff’s office has described its investigation and the alleged pattern of conduct, but the court will determine what evidence is admissible and whether the prosecution meets its burden. Until then, the case should be understood as an accusation involving alleged document fraud and an attempted property-related deception.Why deed fraud is a problemProperty-title fraud often involves making it look like a valid transfer occurred, rather than actually taking possession of a house. Forged signatures, false inheritance claims, unauthorized liens and fraudulent deeds can all create confusion for banks, buyers, title companies and county officials. While such a document, if filed, may not immediately transfer ownership, it can cloud the title and make a future sale or refinance more difficult. This is of particular concern for high value properties where a successful fraud attempt could potentially underpin a large loan application.The Oklahoma Real Estate Commission’s 2026 deed-theft notice identifies several warning signs, including unsolicited mortgage or utility mail, unauthorized deeds, and unexpected loans connected to a property. It advises owners to examine county land records and investigate suspicious notices promptly. Homeowners should also monitor their credit reports for unfamiliar loans and contact the county clerk or an attorney if a deed or lien appears without authorization. Anyone who believes they have been targeted should report the matter to law enforcement.How owners can protect themselvesOklahoma County offers a Property Alert System that sends registered users notifications when documents affecting their property are filed. Alerts can arrive by text message, email, or telephone, giving owners an early warning before a suspicious filing goes unnoticed. The system cannot stop someone from submitting paperwork, but it can help a homeowner respond quickly. In this case, the combination of alert clerk employees, a vigilant homeowner, and law-enforcement involvement appears to have prevented the disputed deed from being recorded.The alleged Oklahoma mansion case is a reminder that ownership is not established by confidence, repeated claims, or a document presented at a counter. It is subject to legal title, to verifiable records and due process. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union road transport minister Nitin Gadkari on Tuesday described the backlash against petrol blended with 20% ethanol (E20) as a “paid campaign”. His remarks came a day after the government notified changes to motor vehicle rules allowing flex-fuel vehicles to run on blends containing up to 100% ethanol.Speaking at an event organised by industry body CII, Gadkari said the opposition to E20 had intensified about three months ago but had since subsided.“Three months ago, huge noise (khub halla) was made against the E20 (20 per cent ethanol-blended petrol) fuel; now rage against E20 fuel is over...It was a paid campaign,” news agency PTI quoted Gadkari as saying.The government on Monday notified amendments to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, permitting flex-fuel vehicles capable of running on fuel containing up to E100, or nearly pure ethanol.Gadkari has repeatedly advocated greater use of ethanol as part of efforts to reduce the country's dependence on imported fossil fuels. He said expanding the use of alternative fuels could help the country save valuable foreign exchange by cutting fossil fuel imports.What was E20 controversy aboutThe Centre’s nationwide rollout of petrol blended with 20% ethanol (E20) had triggered protests and political criticism earlier this year, with motorists raising concerns over reduced mileage and the compatibility of the fuel with older vehicles. Opposition leaders questioned the government’s decision to make E20 the standard fuel at petrol pumps across India in April 2025.The row escalated after attorney general R Venkataramani referred to E20 as an “experiment” during a Supreme Court hearing, saying its results would be known next year. The remark went viral, prompting renewed criticism of the policy.The Centre subsequently clarified that the attorney general was referring to ethanol supply volumes, not describing the E20 policy itself as an experiment. Police launched a search involving a helicopter and a police dog, but the operation had been unsuccessful at the time of reporting. Officers cordoned off the scene on Mecklenhorster Straße to collect evidence.Investigators believe the people involved may have known each other and that the group was deliberately targeted rather than struck at random. However, the motive and the precise circumstances surrounding the incident remain unclear.“The sequence of events and the precise involvement of those involved are still part of the investigation,” the police spokeswoman said, according to NDR.Images and video footage from the scene showed armed police officers, including personnel carrying submachine guns. The abandoned blue BMW reportedly had a flat front tyre. A silver Mercedes with a broken rear window was also seen nearby, although authorities had not established whether it was connected to the incident.Road closures remained in place in parts of Neustadt am Rübenberge, including the stretch between Ludwig-Enneccerus-Platz and Am Schützenplatz, via Herzog-Erich-Allee towards Hannoversche Street, NDR reported.Police are continuing their search for the suspects and investigating the circumstances of the incident. articles.title: Two siblings wanted to buy farmland from their mother’s estate; an Iowa appeals court upheld their removal as executors over self-dealing
articles.summary: Two Iowa siblings were removed as executors of their deceased mother's estate after trying to purchase farmland they were supposed to be managing.
articles.body: Two Iowa siblings were removed as executors of their deceased mother's estate after trying to purchase farmland they were supposed to be managing. The Iowa Court of Appeals upheld the removal, concluding that their proposed transaction created conflict of interest concerns and that they failed to protect the estate's financial interests. In an opinion filed on February 11, 2026, the court also upheld an order directing that the property be sold at public auction, giving the other beneficiaries an opportunity to compete for the land.Iowa court removed two siblings as executors of farmlandThe dispute started after the death of Gloria J. Pflughaupt, who passed away in October 2022. She left her estate to be split equally among her 4 children. The Iowa Court of Appeals said in its opinion in the Matter of the Estate of Gloria J. Pflughaupt that her oldest daughter, Cabrina Bell, and oldest son, James Pflughaupt Jr., were named executors in November 2022.They were responsible for managing the estate and protecting the interests of all 4 beneficiaries. However, disagreements developed over the future of their mother's farmland, which became the central issue in the probate proceedings.The property in Linn County included approximately 104 acres of cropland, another 24 acres of land unsuitable for cultivation and a small homestead. It was the estate's primary asset, making the decision about its sale particularly important to the financial interests of all four siblings.The court found that the older siblings' proposed purchase, combined with their handling of the estate and their strained relationship with the other beneficiaries, justified their removal.How much was the farmland worth and why did the brothers and sisters not agreeIn January 2023, the estate obtained a broker’s price opinion, which valued the property at $1.2 million as of the date of their mother’s death. The broker, knowing the values in the locality, having inspected the farm and compared it with other sales of land, reached this conclusion. It was not a complete appraisal.In April 2023, the executors included this valuation in an estate inventory shared with the beneficiaries.Several months later, the younger siblings, Jordan Pflughaupt and Kimberlee Leopold, proposed buying the interests of their older siblings for $600,000, matching half of the estimated value of the entire farm. They also suggested selling the property at a public auction to allow potential buyers to compete.Cabrina and Jim rejected these proposals without further discussion. Cabrina later testified that they had received other offers that would have generated greater returns, although the court record did not establish the details of those offers.The disagreement deepened when Cabrina and Jim entered into contracts to purchase the property themselves, proposing to divide it into three parcels. One would go to Cabrina, another to Jim, and a third to a neighbouring landowner.The proposed purchase raise concerns about self-dealingThe executors argued that their proposed transaction would bring approximately $1.26 million into the estate, exceeding the original $1.2 million estimate. They also relied on later valuations suggesting that the property could be worth around $1.23 million if marketed separately as cropland and a residential acreage.However, they had not obtained separate valuations for the three parcels they intended to sell. The broker testified that the land had different soil productivity ratings, which could affect the value of each section.Executors seeking to buy property from an estate they oversee must satisfy additional legal requirements because their personal interests might conflict with their duties, the Iowa Court of Appeals said.Such transactions require court approval, after notice to interested parties, under Iowa Code section 633.155. The court can reject a proposed sale if it would disadvantage the estate, and the executors must prove that the transaction serves the estate's interests.Cabrina and Jim acknowledged that their proposal involved self-dealing but maintained that the price was beneficial to the estate. The appeals court, however, found that they had not established that their offer represented the best available deal.What did the court say about the other beneficiaries' offersThe appeals court placed particular emphasis on the executors' failure to explore whether a better sale was possible.Jordan and Kimberlee remained interested in buying the property and were prepared to compete with their older siblings. Jordan testified that he had not been informed about the other offers Cabrina claimed to have received. He also learned about the proposed division of the farm only after the executors submitted their contracts for court approval.Cabrina acknowledged that she had not told her younger siblings that she and Jim intended to purchase the land themselves.The court noted that all 4 children appeared willing to pay more than the property's estimated value. Yet the executors had not established who would offer the highest price because they had not properly explored the available options.The probate court decided that a public auction would be the best way to determine the property's actual market value. The Iowa Court of Appeals agreed, finding no abuse of discretion in rejecting the proposed $1.26 million transaction.Other estate management failures strengthened the case for removalThe court's decision was not based solely on the proposed farmland purchase.The opinion stated the executors gave away hay bales that could have been sold, allowed themselves and others to use the farm without charge and tore down parts of the homestead without consulting Jordan and Kimberlee.The court found that these actions conflicted with the executors' obligation to maximise the estate's value for the beneficiaries.The siblings' relationship also deteriorated during the proceedings. Their hostility was sufficiently pronounced when Cabrina and Jim did not invite their younger siblings to their mother's memorial service. During the court hearing, the judge also had to interrupt proceedings to address the executors' disruptive behaviour.The Iowa Court of Appeals affirmed the probate court's decision to remove Cabrina and Jim as co-executors and appoint an attorney to succeed them. It also upheld the direction that the farmland be sold at public auction and remanded the case for further proceedings.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh CEO Navdeep Rinwa on Tuesday issued an apology for his office's sarcastic reply to Aam Aadmi Party MP Sanjay Singh over
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh CEO Navdeep Rinwa on Tuesday issued an apology for his office's sarcastic reply to Aam Aadmi Party MP Sanjay Singh over allegations of caste bias following an erroneous voter slip entry, saying that the language and tone of the post were not in line with the nature of communication expected from the poll body.The UP CEO said the outrage generated by the social media post had been duly noted and that future communication would be polite and formal."The language, tone, and sharp nature of the comments in the quoted post of this handle are not in line with the nature of communication expected from this official handle. The genuine outrage generated by the comments in the post has been duly noted," the UP CEO said in a post on X."We sincerely apologise to those who are surprised and upset by this. From now on, our communication will be polite and formal," it added.This comes a day after Sanjay Singh questioned Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over an erroneous entry in a voter slip in which "Ramhit Yadav" became "Ram ne Yadav ko Maara".In a post on X in Hindi, Singh said, "Gyanesh Kumar ji, why did Ram hit only a Yadav? Why did Ram not hit any Singh, Pathak, Asthana, Sharma, Rai or Bisht? Is your computer casteist? Are you running the agenda of any political party?"In a sarcastic reply to Singh, the UP CEO's official X handle said that had the entry read that Ram hit a minority, the authorities would have been accused of communalism too."A strange name, 'Ram ne Sharma ko Maara', is also present in the voter list of the recent legislative council elections. Computers/software are not casteist," the UP CEO said."We accept that an error was made, but fortunately, even while making the error, no caste discrimination took place. Thank God that Ram did not hit a minority. Otherwise, besides being accused of casteism, we would have also faced allegations of communalism," it added.The CEO's office also shared a voter slip from the recently held graduate constituency legislative council elections. The slip listed the voter's name as Ravi Sharma, while his father's name appeared as "Ram ne Sharma ko Maara".The exchange comes days after instances of erroneous entries in electoral records were flagged, raising questions over the computer software used to prepare voter lists.Later, UP CEO Navdeep Rinwa, in a post on X, said some "bizarre-looking names" had appeared in the voter list during the recently held legislative council elections."The reasons behind such mistakes are being looked into and appropriate action is being taken to prevent recurrence," the CEO said.He said "some forged voter slips" had gone viral on social media and were being displayed or circulated by several established media outlets and prominent individuals. "The person responsible for the forgery will be dealt with as per law," Rinwa added.Last week, Rinwa had explained that the software was designed to transliterate names entered in English into Hindi.However, in some cases, instead of transliterating names, it translated the words, resulting in incorrect entries. For instance, if "Ramhit Yadav" was mistakenly typed as "Ram Hit Yadav", the software translated it into Hindi as "Ram ne Yadav ko Maara" (Ram hit Yadav). He said the errors could have been corrected using the editing feature, but some remained in the final list.Another instance, in which "B.Com" was entered in place of the father's name in the electoral roll for the legislative council polls, appeared to be a case of human error or negligence, the CEO had said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2010, a collector paid $7.36 million for a 2,000-year-old Roman emperor's marble torso; after years on display at major US museums, the headless sculpture sold in New York for $34.26 million in October 2026
articles.summary: A headless marble torso of a Roman emperor, which sold for $7.36 million in 2010 and was subsequently displayed at several major museums across the United
articles.body: A headless marble torso of a Roman emperor, which sold for $7.36 million in 2010 and was subsequently displayed at several major museums across the United States, has fetched $34.26 million at an auction in New York. The nearly 2,000-year-old sculpture was offered at Sotheby's Magnum Opus evening auction on October 21, 2026, achieving a price significantly higher than its previous sale and setting a record for a Roman antiquity sold at auction, according to Artnet News.Reportedly 5 collectors competed for the sculpture during bidding that reportedly lasted 14 minutes. This result surpassed the previous auction record for a Roman antiquity, highlighting the demand and how factors such as provenance, rarity, artistic attributes and historical significance can all together influence the price of an antiquity and the competition among prospective buyers.The sale marks a substantial increase in the sculpture's market value over 16 years, with its latest price nearly approaching 5 times the amount paid by the previous buyer. The sculpture has traversed a journey through private ownership and prominent museum exhibitions, garnering renewed attention.What is the marble torso’s history?According to Sotheby's catalogue, the sculpture dates to the first half of the first century AD and belongs to the Julio-Claudian period of Roman history. Its precise identity remains uncertain, although it has been suggested that the figure could represent Augustus, Tiberius or Claudius, all three emperors associated with the early Roman Empire.The breastplate features a relief of Sol, the Roman sun god, emerging from the waters in a chariot drawn by four horses. Other decorative details include figures of Victory, shields, a trophy and floral motifs. Such imagery was commonly used in Roman imperial art to associate rulers with military achievement, divine favour and political authority.Furthermore, Sotheby's has noted that the sculpture originated in Salona, an ancient Roman city in present day Croatia. Sotheby's notes that it perhaps came from the vicinity of two temples near the northeastern corner of the city's forum. While the marble itself is believed to have been sourced from the Greek island of Paros, which was renowned for its fine quality marble.The sculpture's journey through American museumsFollowing its 2010 sale, the marble torso was exhibited at some of the United States' leading cultural institutions. It appeared at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York between 2011 and 2013, before being displayed at Yale University Art Gallery in New Haven from 2013 to 2015. The sculpture subsequently returned to the Metropolitan Museum of Art from 2015 to 2017 and was later exhibited at the J. Paul Getty Museum in Los Angeles between 2021 and 2024.These exhibitions placed the sculpture before museum audiences over several years, allowing visitors to encounter a work of Roman imperial art outside a private collection. Its appearances at these institutions also form a significant part of its more recent history, preceding its return to the international auction market in October 2026. Although the sculpture has lost its head, much of its intricate marble surface has been preserved. .A record-breaking result at Sotheby'sThe torso's October 2026 sale represents a considerable change from its previous appearance at auction in 2010, when it fetched $7.36 million. Its latest price of $34.26 million places it among the most valuable examples of ancient Roman sculpture sold on the international art market.The sculpture’s journey through museums and exhibitions to now its latest sale adds another chapter to its long history, taking it from the world of ancient Roman imperial art through private collections to a record breaking auction in New York.You use AI every day. articles.title: Kate Middleton climbed Britain's three highest peaks within 24 hours in June to support a cancer charity; four months later, she shared an unseen photo with William, their three children and mountain rescuers
articles.summary: Kate Middleton, on Sunday, shared a new family photograph from a mountain climbing challenge she completed four months ago to support a cancer charity.
articles.body: Kate Middleton, on Sunday, shared a new family photograph from a mountain climbing challenge she completed four months ago to support a cancer charity. The Princess of Wales's Instagram post shows her with her husband, Prince William, their three children, and mountain rescue volunteers who were present during the event. Kate shared the photograph to mark Mountain Rescue Awareness Day and thank the people who help keep walkers and climbers safe.In the photograph, Kate, 44, and William, also 44, are standing outdoors with Prince George, 13, Princess Charlotte, 11, and Prince Louis, 8. According to Town & Country magazine, the picture was taken at the base of Snowdon, also known as Yr Wyddfa in Welsh, during the weekend of June 27–28. Members of a local mountain rescue team are also seen with the family, along with a golden retriever wearing a red coat.The Princess had shared other family pictures from the challenge in July, but this photograph had not been made public until now. The June challenge was particularly important to Kate because she had undergone cancer treatment.Kate's mountain challenge and her cancer remissionIn January 2025, Kate announced that her cancer was in remission. A few months later, she decided to take part in the climbing challenge to support The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity. According to Town & Country magazine, the charity supports the hospital where she received cancer treatment in 2024.In late June, Kate took on the task of climbing three of Britain's highest mountains in just 24 hours. The route included Ben Nevis in Scotland, Scafell Pike in England and Snowdon in Wales. Together, they make up the National Three Peaks Challenge.On July 5, a few days after completing the challenge, she shared photographs showing her with William and their children. In those pictures, she could be seen embracing her family after finishing the climbs.Along with the photographs, Kate spoke about why she had chosen to take part. She explained that the challenge was “not simply a physical endeavor”, but also a “chance to explore life beyond diagnosis and to give something back.”In September, Kate also hosted a small tea party at Windsor Castle for other people who had taken part in the Three Peaks Challenge and their families. According to Town & Country magazine, she spoke about the participants' experiences in a social media statement following the gathering. She said their stories showed how important it was to have support from others during recovery.“Behind every summit was a personal story of resilience, determination and hope,” Kate said in her statement. She also spoke about how listening to the participants had reminded her that recovery was rarely something people went through alone.Kate thanks volunteers who help people in the mountainsIn her October 25 Instagram post, Kate spoke about the people who volunteer to help walkers and climbers when they need assistance in the mountains.She said that she and William had seen the dedication of these teams through their association with the organisation. She also praised the care and professionalism with which the volunteers carry out their work.Kate recalled meeting local rescue teams during the Three Peaks Challenge in June. She said the experience gave her an opportunity to thank them personally for helping people stay safe throughout the year.“Meeting local mountain rescue teams during the Three Peaks Challenge this summer was an opportunity to say thank you in person for the vital role they play in keeping walkers and climbers safe on the mountains all year round,” she wrote.The Princess also said she was “incredibly proud to support the extraordinary volunteers” and expressed her appreciation for their courage and service.Although Kate shared the photograph, the message came from both her and William. The couple signed the post together, thanking the rescue teams for the work they continue to do.Why Kate and William shared the photograph in OctoberThe timing of the post was linked to Mountain Rescue Awareness Day, which is observed during the final week of October in Britain.This is also the period when clocks go back in the UK and evenings start getting darker earlier. According to Mountain Rescue England and Wales, the awareness day reminds people to take care when visiting mountainous areas, particularly as daylight hours become shorter.The organisation has a longstanding connection with Prince William. He became its patron in 2007 and has held the role for nearly two decades.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
