articles.title: $445 million and counting: Elon Musk goes all in for Republicans ahead of US midterms
articles.summary: Elon Musk has contributed more than $445 million to political groups during the current US election cycle, emerging as one of the biggest-ever donors to
articles.body: Elon Musk has contributed more than $445 million to political groups during the current US election cycle, emerging as one of the biggest-ever donors to super political action committees (super PACs), according to a report.Musk’s donations have helped widen the Republican Party’s fundraising advantage ahead of the November midterm elections, which are projected to be the most expensive elections ever in the US.Federal Election Commission (FEC) filings show Musk contributed $77 million to America PAC in the first two weeks of October. Since relaunching the political group in July, he has given it $355 million, averaging $3.6 million a day, Bloomberg reported.The Republican Party, its congressional super PACs and US president Donald Trump’s MAGA Inc. had raised $2.1 billion through October 14, compared with $1.4 billion raised by corresponding Democratic committees.Musk’s political spending has supported Republican candidates across several contests, including the Texas Senate race involving Attorney General Ken Paxton and Democratic candidate James Talarico. His America PAC has also spent money on voter outreach through canvassing, digital media, text messages and printed material.Talarico’s campaign has criticised the billionaire’s financial influence. An advertisement released by the campaign said: “He knows that if his millions drag the most corrupt politician in Texas across the finish line, Ken Paxton will owe him everything. So let’s remind Elon: Texas is not for sale.”On Friday, Trump said on Truth Social he planned to spend $400 million to $500 million by election day, then less than two weeks away. Filings show $225 million of recent spending went through super PACs No Going Back and Safety & Affordability.Meanwhile, Reuters reported that Republican megadonors, including Stephen Wynn, Stephen Schwarzman and Diane Hendricks, contributed millions to Trump-aligned MAGA Inc., which had raised roughly $450 million this cycle and held $164 million in available cash.What are the US election contribution limits?US federal election law sets limits on how much individuals and political committees can contribute directly to candidates and certain political organisations. However, super PACs operate under different rules and can accept unlimited contributions. This distinction helps explain how Musk can give hundreds of millions of dollars to political groups despite restrictions on direct donations to candidates.According to the US Federal Election Commission’s (FEC) limits for the 2025–2026 election cycle, individuals can contribute up to $3,500 per election to a federal candidate. The limit applies separately to each election, so the primary and general elections have separate limits.Individuals can contribute up to $5,000 per year to a conventional political action committee (PAC), $10,000 annually in combined contributions to state, district and local party committees, and $44,300 per year to each national party committee. They can also contribute up to $132,900 per year to each eligible additional national party account, earmarked for specific expenses such as presidential nominating conventions, election recounts and legal proceedings and party headquarters buildings, under the Federal Election Commission’s 2025–2026 limits.Super PACs, formally known as independent-expenditure-only committees, can accept unlimited contributions from individuals, corporations, labour organisations and other political committees to fund independent political spending. However, they cannot contribute directly to federal candidates, and their spending must not be coordinated with candidates’ campaigns.Why Musk’s donations matterMusk has substantial business interests in companies including Tesla and SpaceX, which are subject to federal regulation. Bloomberg reported that his political spending could also influence the balance of power in Congress, particularly if Democrats win control of the House of Representatives.You use AI every day. articles.title: Karnataka loses nearly 1 crore voters after SIR, final electorate stands at 4.54 crore; 65.45 lakh marked permanently shifted
articles.summary: BENGALURU: The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Karnataka concluded on October 27, with the state losing about 99.76 lakh voters from its original
articles.body: BENGALURU: The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Karnataka concluded on October 27, with the state losing about 99.76 lakh voters from its original electorate of 5.5 crore, bringing the total electorate to 4,54,55,689 (or 4.54 crore).About 86.56 lakh of these voters are in the 20-29 age group, while the number of new voters stands at 6.83 lakh.As of June 16, when the rolls were frozen for the SIR process, the state had about 5.5 crore voters. However, during the subsequent enumeration phase, which resulted in the August 24 draft list, about 19.48% or 1.08 crore voters were removed after being categorised as ASDDO (Absent, shifted, dead, duplicate and others).The largest chunk of voters removed from the draft list were those classified as 'permanently shifted'. This category accounted for 65.45 lakh voters, or 11.8% of the ASDDO list.The total number of people who made it to the final list after the notices phase was 43.2 lakh out of 43.82 lakh, with 61,867 voters excluded from the final list following the notices.The state has the largest number of voters between the age of 30 to 39 years of age, accounting for 1.02 cr of the 4.5 cr voters at present. At 2.29 voters, there are four lakh more female voters to their male counterparts in Karnataka.The two-month claims, notices and objections phase, which began on August 24, saw about 43.8 lakh of the 4.4 crore voters on the draft list (4,46,35,975) being issued notices. Officials said about 60,000 of them were excluded from the final list. Claims and objections could be filed only during the first month of this phase, until September 23.Between June 16 and September 23, 7.87 lakh citizens sought inclusion in the final voter list through Form 6 applications, while 4,530 NRIs sought inclusion through Form 6A. Objections to existing voters and requests for deletion, filed either by voters themselves or their families, amounted to 58,475.Meanwhile, 10.99 lakh voters from the draft list sought modifications to their details, ranging from spelling corrections to changes in polling booth locations.The SIR exercise in the state began on June 20, with the deployment of 59,050 booth-level officers (BLOs), 332 Assistant Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs) and 224 Electoral Registration Officers (EROs). There were 5,905 BLO supervisors, each overseeing 10 BLOs. The district commissioners were designated as District Election Officers (DEOs), with 34 such officers across the state.The number of BLOs and AEROs increased over time to 60,932 and 4,258, respectively.Recognised political parties appointed 1.33 lakh booth-level agents (BLAs) during the enumeration phase to ensure the forms reached voters. These BLAs were also instrumental in filing objections against voters on the list during the subsequent claims and objections period.The enumeration phase began on June 30 and was granted two extensions. While it was originally scheduled to end on July 29, the CEO's office announced a 10-day extension to August 8 on July 15, owing to the large number of voters requiring ASDDO classification. articles.body: DJ Akademiks has shared his thoughts on Kai Cenat’s legal fight with his former friend Reggie Travers, warning that the case could bring difficult questions for the Twitch star. During a recent livestream, Akademiks explained that taking someone to court could also mean answering questions about personal and business matters. He pointed to Kai’s business, girlfriend, and the time spent at the Clover Boys house. Akademiks believes the legal move could hurt Kai if parts of his own story do not hold up.DJ Akademiks warns Kai Cenat could face questions about his private lifeDuring his stream, Akademiks explained why he thinks Kai could face problems as the legal fight moves forward. articles.title: A California restaurant raised a record $75,000 for children battling cancer by selling more than 60,000 cookies; the money will revamp a programme supporting young patients
articles.summary: A California restaurant has raised a record-breaking $75,000 for children battling cancer by selling more than 60,000 cookies during a month-long
articles.body: A California restaurant has raised a record-breaking $75,000 for children battling cancer by selling more than 60,000 cookies during a month-long fundraising campaign. Corky’s Kitchen & Bakery collected the money through its annual Cookies for Cancer initiative, which supports patients receiving care at Loma Linda University Children’s Hospital in California. The restaurant raised nearly $25,000 more than it did in 2025, marking an increase of more than 48% across its 13 outlets. The hospital announced the achievement on October 26, 2026, following the presentation of a cheque to its administration and staff on October 20. The latest contribution will help revamp the hospital’s Beads of Courage programme, which recognises and celebrates the experiences of children undergoing cancer treatment.California’s Corky’s Kitchen & Bakery raises record $75,000The fundraiser took place throughout September, which is recognised in the US as Childhood Cancer Awareness Month. Customers at Corky’s Kitchen & Bakery could purchase gold ribbon-shaped cookies or regular cookies, with a portion of the proceeds going towards the hospital’s paediatric haematology and oncology services. Customers could also make direct cash donations.The campaign brought in more than $75,000, exceeding the restaurant’s target. Darin Handlen, Corky’s director of operations, said the team had aimed to raise 10% more than the previous year, but the final total surpassed expectations.According to the hospital’s announcement, the restaurant raised nearly $25,000 more than in 2025, representing year-on-year growth of more than 48%.More than 60,000 cookies sold during SeptemberThe scale of the campaign was reflected in the work involved. Corky’s employees made and sold more than 60,000 cookies during September, using 208 pounds of gold sprinkles as part of the effort.The restaurant’s official campaign page said it donated $1.25 for every gold ribbon cookie sold and 50 cents for every other cookie sold. The fundraiser also invited customers to support the cause through direct donations.The campaign ran across the chain’s 13 outlets, the same number of stores involved in the previous year’s effort. The combination of cookie sales and additional contributions helped the restaurant reach its highest fundraising total for the initiative.Where the $75,000 donation will goThe money will benefit patients receiving care through Loma Linda University Children’s Hospital’s paediatric haematology and oncology services. Scarlett Czarnecki, director of patient care for the hospital’s Pediatric Hematology/Oncology Service Line and Child Life Department, said the funds would be used to revamp the Beads of Courage programme.The programme helps hospital staff recognise and celebrate the journeys of children undergoing cancer treatment. It provides a way to acknowledge the experiences and milestones young patients encounter during their care.The hospital’s announcement identifies the programme as the planned use of this year’s funds. The donation should therefore not be described as being specifically allocated to cancer research or medical equipment.An 11-year tradition of supporting young patientsThe Cookies for Cancer initiative has been running for 11 years. With the latest contribution, Corky’s Kitchen & Bakery has donated more than $315,000 to Loma Linda University Children’s Hospital through the campaign over that period.The fundraiser has grown considerably over time. In 2025, the restaurant raised more than $51,000, according to its official campaign page. This year’s total of more than $75,000 represents a substantial increase on that amount.The initiative has become a recurring way for the restaurant to involve customers and employees in supporting children receiving cancer care.Restaurant also organises activities for children receiving treatmentCorky’s involvement extends beyond raising money. In August 2026, the restaurant organised a cookie-decorating activity for children receiving cancer treatment at the hospital for the second consecutive year.The event gave young patients an opportunity to decorate freshly baked cookies using supplies provided by the restaurant. Corky’s also runs an Art for Cancer initiative, through which children can colour pictures or create encouraging messages that are delivered to patients at the hospital.These activities complement the fundraising campaign by offering creative experiences for children and families dealing with the demands of cancer treatment.How the Cookies for Cancer campaign worksThe annual campaign combines everyday purchases with charitable giving. During September, customers can buy cookies at Corky’s outlets, with different donation amounts attached to gold ribbon cookies and other varieties. Direct contributions are also accepted.The gold ribbon is commonly associated with childhood cancer awareness, making it a fitting symbol for the fundraiser. The restaurant’s campaign also encourages children to participate through artwork and messages of support for young hospital patients.By involving customers, staff and children in different ways, the initiative has developed into a community effort that supports the hospital’s work with young patients. Its latest record donation will help the hospital continue the Beads of Courage programme for children undergoing treatment.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: A 45-year-old teacher in Russia's Dagestan region has spent nine years walking 14 kilometres through mountainous terrain every day to reach a school where
articles.body: A 45-year-old teacher in Russia's Dagestan region has spent nine years walking 14 kilometres through mountainous terrain every day to reach a school where just three children study. Khadijat Magomedova, who serves as both the head of Khonok Primary School and its only teacher, reportedly takes around four hours to complete the daily journey to and from work. The school is located in the Shamil district, at an altitude of approximately 1,800 metres above sea level. Her route involves descending one mountain and climbing another, with steep paths and rocky terrain making the commute difficult. After a video documenting her journey attracted attention online, residents suggested organising a fundraiser to buy her a car or horse to make the journey easier.A four-hour journey through Dagestan's mountainsMagomedova's daily commute covers approximately seven kilometres each way, according to a report by Caucasian Knot published on October 26, 2026. The journey takes around two hours in each direction, meaning she spends approximately four hours walking to and from the school.Her village and workplace are situated on different mountains. She reportedly leaves home at around 7 am, descends approximately 400 metres and then climbs towards the mountain where the school is located.The route is not an ordinary walk along a paved road. It involves difficult mountain terrain, making the journey physically demanding. Despite the challenges, Magomedova has continued the commute for nine years to teach the children at the remote school.The teacher has encountered a wolf and a rockfallThe difficult terrain has exposed Magomedova to natural hazards. In a video shared on October 24 by the Instagram account makhachkala_, she recalled encountering a wolf during her journey.She described hearing the animal howl before seeing it sitting in a clearing. According to Caucasian Knot, the encounter ended without injury, and the wolf returned to the mountains.Magomedova also recalled experiencing a significant rockfall along the route. These incidents illustrate the challenges she faces while travelling between the villages, although reports do not establish how frequently such encounters occur.The teacher has continued making the journey despite these experiences. Her story gained wider attention after blogger Semyon Rasputin documented her commute and shared details about the school's circumstances.She is the school's director and only teacherMagomedova heads Khonok Primary School in the village of Khonok in Dagestan's Shamil district. She is also the school's only teacher, responsible for teaching all subjects to its three pupils.According to the reports, the school has two classes attended by two boys and a girl. Children from different grades study simultaneously in the same classroom, allowing lessons to continue despite the small number of students.Her responsibilities therefore extend beyond teaching. As the school's director, she also heads the institution, making her central to its continued operation.The available reports do not provide details about the school's budget, staffing arrangements or whether authorities have considered alternative transport options for her commute.Residents suggest buying her a car or horseMagomedova's story prompted an outpouring of responses on social media, with residents calling for practical assistance to make her daily journey easier.Some users suggested that the authorities should increase her salary and arrange transport. Others proposed organising a fundraiser to purchase a car or horse so that she could travel to school more easily.Caucasian Knot reported that these suggestions emerged in response to the video documenting her journey. The proposals reflect public concern about the difficulties she faces while travelling through the mountains to teach the children.Magomedova's experience highlights the challenges of providing education in remote mountain communities, where difficult geography and limited transport can make access to schools complicated.You use AI every day. articles.title: Meet Disha Daga, the 26-year-old Pune woman who began drawing mandalas in her notebooks without studying art and went on to paint for the RBI, work with major brands and teach over 25,000 students
articles.summary: At 26, Pune-based artist Disha Daga has taken her mandala designs from the margins of college notebooks to the walls of the Reserve Bank of India’s Pune
articles.body: At 26, Pune-based artist Disha Daga has taken her mandala designs from the margins of college notebooks to the walls of the Reserve Bank of India’s Pune office. She has worked with corporate clients, created murals outside India and taught thousands of people, despite never having formally studied art.Her journey began in 2016, when she was looking for a hobby beyond dance. As reported by The Indian Express, Daga came across mehendi designs on Pinterest and began drawing similar patterns in her notebooks. She did not initially know what the intricate circular designs were called. A Google search introduced her to mandalas.A mandala is a pattern built around a central point, often with shapes and designs radiating outwards. The word comes from the Sanskrit term for “circle”, and mandalas have traditionally been associated with the representation of the universe.From college notebooks to commissioned artworkAccording to The Indian Express, Daga continued drawing while studying at Wadia College in Pune and managing her degree, diploma courses and dance. But the time she spent making mandalas gradually became more than a pastime. “It makes you patient,” she said, describing how working through each layer required concentration and taught her to slow down. She did not initially plan to become a professional artist. The change came in 2020, when the pandemic shut colleges and cancelled events. Tired of working on paper, she decided to paint a mandala on a wall at home.After she posted the artwork online, people began asking her to create designs for them. Her first commercial project came in August 2021. Daga now works under the name Disha Draws. According to the official website of MyTribe, she transitioned from a commerce background to a full-time art practice, with commissioned murals and workshops becoming key parts of her work.Her artwork reaches the RBI and international clientsOne of Daga’s recent government commissions was a large mandala painting at the Reserve Bank of India’s Pune office, displayed near the entrance. Her work has also reached Malaysia, Thailand and the United States. According to The Indian Express, her clients have included a consumer electronics brand, a global car manufacturer, an investment firm and Vantara, the wildlife centre in Jamnagar.Her workshop listings describe sessions in which participants learn mandala techniques through guided, hands-on practice. Artoreal, which features her work for sale, describes Daga as a Pune-based mandala artist, muralist and art educator. The platform says she has created more than 120 large-scale mandala artworks for homes, offices, commercial spaces and public settings, with work delivered internationally.Teaching more than 25,000 studentsAlongside commissioned artwork, Daga conducts online and offline workshops. She told The Indian Express that these have reached more than 25,000 students. Her work as an educator also has an independent institutional record. The National Book Trust of India’s 2023-24 annual report lists a mandala art workshop conducted by Disha Dinesh Daga for children on December 18, 2023.She has also built quite an audience on social media. Her Instagram account (@dishadrawss) has more than 42,000 followers.The financial uncertainty behind an art careerBuilding an independent art practice has its own challenges. Daga says income can fluctuate because it depends on commissions, exhibitions, workshops and the ability to reach prospective clients. Quieter periods can be difficult to manage. Artists must also handle work beyond creating art, including marketing, client communication, negotiations and project management. Daga believes artists need to understand the basics of running a business, even when they hire professionals to help with some responsibilities.She also believes art should be treated as a profession that deserves fair compensation and financial security, rather than being seen only as a passion.Daga hopes her journey will encourage young people to question the idea that success must follow academic achievements or conventional career paths. Her own career developed through a hobby she pursued without formal art training, eventually opening doors to commissioned projects, international work and teaching. Her advice to young people is to build their own paths, even when the journey feels uncertain.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ testGet the latest Lifestyle News and more. articles.summary: Beyoncé’s charity foundation has awarded $50,000 to In a Perfect World, a non-profit organisation focused on youth education, creativity, social
articles.body: Beyoncé’s charity foundation has awarded $50,000 to In a Perfect World, a non-profit organisation focused on youth education, creativity, social consciousness and leadership, according to a report by Black Enterprise. The grant will help the organisation expand its educational and leadership programmes, allowing it to reach hundreds more young people.Building leaders ‘In a Perfect World’Founded and led by Manuela Testolini, In a Perfect World runs programmes that teach young people to lead and take part in civic life. Two of its main initiatives are Youth Ambassadors and REACH, which supports schools and educational resources. The organisation focuses on giving students responsibility, not just lessons, and that is the point Testolini returns to most often.The organisation says its work has supported 35 school projects across eight countries. It has also worked in more than 500 classrooms in high-poverty areas and logged 20,000 hours of service led by young people. Taken together, it says, those efforts have touched 50,000 lives around the world.“One of the things I’m most proud of is taking young leaders from the United States to Central America to build schools for indigenous communities there, to build with them. They’re young leaders here, but how do they take what they’re doing across borders? How do they help other young people find their voice and have their place in the world?” Testolini said.The timing of the $50,000 grant is also crucial. It arrives as schools and community programmes face tighter budgets. “This very generous grant is going to allow us to expand programming to hundreds more kids who need our support. Between all of the cuts to education, cuts to after-school programming, creative programming, we are so needed right now, and this could not come at a better time,” Testolini said.She expects the money to allow the organisation to expand its programmes to hundreds more children who need support. The grant does not solve the underlying shortfall, but it gives one group room to grow.Beyoncé’s BeyGoodBeyoncé Knowles-Carter started the BeyGood foundation in 2013. The charity considers education, entrepreneurship and community response its three core pillars. Its broader aim is economic equity, meaning people should be able to access the opportunities they need to build something for themselves.“On behalf of Mrs Beyoncé Knowles-Carter and Ms Tina Knowles, we are just grateful for you to be in this ecosystem now because, again, we see the good work you’re doing, and we know that you will continue to do it without a doubt,” said Allana J. Barefield, BeyGood’s digital editorial content manager, in a video shared on Instagram.Since its launch, BeyGood has supported a range of causes, from relief efforts for those affected by the Los Angeles wildfires and Florida hurricanes to educational initiatives such as the Beyoncé Knowles-Carter x Lorraine Schwartz GIA Scholarship. It has also backed other groups, including through a $100,000 gift to Texas Southern University’s Ocean of Soul Marching Band and $120,000 in grants to small businesses in Atlanta.You use AI every day. articles.title: A World War II bunker in England with four-foot-thick walls has been transformed into a £650,000 two-bedroom home with a rooftop terrace and modern interiors
articles.summary: A World War II bunker in Oxfordshire, England, has been transformed into a two-bedroom home with a rooftop terrace, skylights and modern interiors,
articles.body: A World War II bunker in Oxfordshire, England, has been transformed into a two-bedroom home with a rooftop terrace, skylights and modern interiors, despite originally having four-foot-thick walls and no windows. According to The Sun, known as The Bunker, the former RAF shelter near Bicester was converted in 2014 and listed for sale for £650,000 in April 2026. The property retains its original red-brick exterior and features such as earth mounds that once offered protection against blasts. Inside, an open-plan kitchen and living area, bi-fold doors and a decked terrace have replaced the building’s former utilitarian layout, while its military history remains visible in its distinctive exterior.How did a WWII bunker become a two-bedroom homeThe bunker’s original design included thick walls and a windowless layout. articles.title: A £15 million London apartment linked to a Bangladeshi businessman was frozen by the High Court after shares in its owning company were reportedly transferred for £1
articles.summary: A luxury apartment near Regent’s Park in London has been frozen by the High Court while the UK’s National Crime Agency (NCA) investigates the source of
articles.body: A luxury apartment near Regent’s Park in London has been frozen by the High Court while the UK’s National Crime Agency (NCA) investigates the source of the money used to acquire it. The property, valued at about £15 million, is linked to Bangladeshi businessman Anisuzzaman “Ronny” Chowdhury, brother of the country’s former land minister. The case centres on a reported September 2025 transaction in which shares in the company holding the apartment were transferred to a third party for a nominal £1, although the NCA valued the transaction at £14.95 million. Investigators allege that the arrangement was intended to conceal Chowdhury’s continued control of the property and facilitate the refinancing of loans secured against it. Mrs Justice Karen Steyn found a good arguable case that the apartment represented the proceeds of crime and granted a property freezing order. Chowdhury did not oppose the application, denied wrongdoing and said he would defend any civil recovery proceedings.Why a London apartment worth £15 million was frozenAccording to the Financial Times, Land Registry records show that Chowdhury purchased the apartment in 2023 for £12.4 million through a company called Ronny 42 Limited. The NCA subsequently investigated the funding behind the purchase as part of wider inquiries into suspected embezzlement, corruption, fraud and money laundering connected to assets associated with his family. In 2025, Chowdhury became subject to an unexplained wealth order (UWO), requiring him to explain the source of the funds used to acquire the property. Similar orders were obtained in connection with his brother, Saifuzzaman Chowdhury, Bangladesh’s former land minister, as well as the former minister’s wife and associated companies.The NCA later applied for a property freezing order to prevent the apartment from being sold or transferred while its investigation continued. At the High Court hearing, Mrs Justice Karen Steyn found a good arguable case that the property represented the proceeds of crime and granted the order. This is a finding that the legal threshold for the order was met, not a final determination that the property was criminal proceeds. Chowdhury’s legal representatives did not oppose the application. Speaking to the Financial Times, he denied attempting to conceal his ownership and said the property had been transparently disclosed to investigators. He also said he had “no business relation” with his brother and denied that his wife and children were involved in the matter. He said he would vigorously defend any civil recovery proceedings brought by the NCA. The agency’s evidence described the apartment as Chowdhury’s principal UK residence. The property remains subject to the court’s order while the investigation and any subsequent recovery proceedings continue.The reported £1 share transfer and the DBS loan disputeThe company transaction is central to the investigation. In September 2025, shares in the company holding the apartment, renamed PNN UK Properties, were reportedly transferred to a third party for £1. The NCA valued the wider transaction at £14.95 million, close to the apartment’s estimated market value. In submissions to the court, the NCA described the transfer as an “arrangement of convenience” connected to refinancing loans secured against the apartment from Singapore-based DBS Bank. The agency alleged that the structure was intended to facilitate refinancing while concealing Chowdhury’s continued control of the property and allowing his wife and 2 daughters to regain control.The court also heard that the loans had not been refinanced and that DBS was pursuing repossession following a loan default. The NCA’s concerns about the ownership arrangements and the outstanding lending formed part of the case for freezing the property. The reported £1 price needs to be distinguished from the agency’s valuation of the transaction as a whole. A company can own a property while its shares change hands, meaning that the property may remain registered in the company’s name even as control of the company changes. Investigators therefore examine the underlying ownership arrangements, the financial purpose of a transfer and who ultimately benefits from it. The allegations about the transaction have not been finally determined through civil recovery proceedings. Chowdhury has denied wrongdoing and said he intends to challenge the allegations against him.How unexplained wealth orders work in the UKUnexplained wealth orders are investigative tools available under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002. They allow specified enforcement authorities to require individuals or companies to explain the source of funds used to acquire particular assets when the statutory conditions are met. Under the legislation, failure to comply with a UWO without reasonable excuse creates a rebuttable presumption, in subsequent civil recovery proceedings, that the property is recoverable. This does not automatically transfer ownership to the state or establish criminal guilt. The authorities must pursue the relevant legal process to recover an asset.A property freezing order serves a different purpose: it prevents the property from being sold or otherwise dealt with while the investigation or civil recovery process proceeds. The NCA has used unexplained wealth orders in other high-value property investigations. In 2019, it obtained orders concerning properties in London linked to individuals associated with a former Kazakh government official. However, in National Crime Agency v Baker, the High Court discharged the relevant unexplained wealth orders and related interim freezing orders on April 8, 2020, after finding that the statutory requirements had not been met. The case illustrates that these investigative powers remain subject to judicial scrutiny.In the Regent’s Park case, the next steps will depend on the evidence concerning the source of the purchase funds, the company’s share transfer and the outstanding DBS loans. The property freezing order preserves the apartment while the investigation continues, but the ultimate question of whether it can be recovered as criminal property remains to be resolved through the civil process.You use AI every day. articles.title: Days after Rubio's visit, Centre says 'under no pressure' to stop buying Russian oil
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Union petroleum minister Hardeep Singh Puri on Tuesday said that India was not under any pressure to stop buying Russian oil.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union petroleum minister Hardeep Singh Puri on Tuesday said that India was not under any pressure to stop buying Russian oil.During an interaction at the 29th Energy Technology and Innovation Meet, Puri said Indian refiners would purchase crude from suppliers offering the most competitive prices as the country prioritises energy security amid global market uncertainties."I have never felt any pressure," Puri said during the interaction at the 29th Energy Technology and Innovation Meet, which began here on Tuesday."India was not particularly buying Russian oil at present, but the decisions in this regard were guided by commercial considerations rather than pressure from any country," he added."At the point of negotiation, whoever is supplying a particular grade, we will buy from them. Prices come down sometimes," he further said.Puri also said India had diversified its energy investments and sourcing, adding that New Delhi's approach was guided by the need to ensure reliable supplies while managing costs for consumers and the broader economy."India had diversified its energy investments and sourcing," the minister said."India, as a major energy-consuming nation, could not compromise on its energy security amid geopolitical developments and volatility in international markets," he added.Puri's remarks come days after US secretary of state Marco Rubio visited India against the backdrop of US’ Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act meant to penalise countries purchasing Russian oil and Trump’s subsequent suspension temporarily of related tariffs.Rubio also said US was in discussions with Reliance Industries on creating capacity to refine Venezuelan crude, calling India a refining superpower and underlining that Washington understood India’s need to diversify its oil imports and saw Venezuela as a potential source of supply.Rubio said New Delhi had repeatedly expressed its desire to diversify its energy portfolio, describing it as a sensible strategy.“In the end, it’s not just about Russian oil; it’s about their desire to diversify,” he said, adding US was keen to be a source of energy supplies for India.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: US midterms: Trump's Republicans may lose control of Congress; what betting markets are saying
articles.summary: With just a week left for the US midterm elections, betting markets suggest that President Donald Trump's Republican Party could lose control of Congress.
articles.body: With just a week left for the US midterm elections, betting markets suggest that President Donald Trump's Republican Party could lose control of Congress. Democrats have strong chances to win the House of Representatives, while the race for the Senate remains tighter.According to prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket, Democrats have a roughly 90% chance of taking control of the House of Representatives. Their chances of winning the Senate are lower, at around 65%.The November 3 elections will decide which party controls the two chambers of Congress for the remaining two years of Trump's presidency. Republicans currently control both, giving the president an advantage in pushing through his policies.House: Democrats ahead in betting marketsAll 435 seats in the House of Representatives will be up for election on November 3. A party needs at least 218 seats to secure a majority.According to Kalshi's October 26 figures, Democrats have a 91% chance of winning control of the House, compared with 9% for Republicans. Polymarket shows a similar trend, giving Democrats a 92% chance.The numbers have also changed over the past few months. In May, Kalshi projected that Democrats would win around 226 seats. By October 26, that figure had risen to 238, well above the majority mark.Senate: A closer contestThe race for the Senate is tighter, although betting markets give Democrats an advantage here also.According to Kalshi, Democrats have a 63% chance of taking control of the Senate, while Polymarket puts their chances at 66%.Unlike the House, where all seats are contested, 35 Senate seats are up for election this year, including special elections. Republicans currently hold 53 seats, while Democrats and independents who caucus with them hold 47.To win, Democrats need to gain control of Republican-held seats while retaining those they already have.Kalshi's latest figures give Democrats a 73% chance of winning in Alaska, 68% in Ohio and 66% in Texas. In Maine, their chances stand at 59%.In June, Kalshi put Democrats' chances of taking control at less than 43%. By late October, that figure had climbed to around 65%.Vivek Ramaswamy's Ohio contestThe betting markets are also tracking the Ohio governor's race, where Indian-American Republican Vivek Ramaswamy is contesting against Democrat's Amy Acton.According to the latest figures, Kalshi gave Ramaswamy a 18% chance of winning, compared with 82% for Acton. Polymarket showed similar numbers, putting Ramaswamy at 18% and Acton at 83%.Ramaswamy, who previously ran for the Republican presidential nomination, is seeking to succeed Mike DeWine, who cannot contest another consecutive term.The Ohio governor's race is separate from the battle for control of Congress, but will also be decided on November 3.What are the possible outcomes?Beyond individual races, prediction markets are tracking the chances of each party controlling Congress after the election.According to Kalshi, traders put the chances of Democrats winning both chambers at 64%, while Polymarket puts the figure at around 66%.The possibility of Democrats winning the House while Republicans retaining the Senate stands at 28% on Kalshi and 27% on Polymarket.A Republican victory in both chambers is given a much lower chance, at 9.3% on Kalshi and 8% on Polymarket.What do the numbers mean for TrumpRepublicans currently control both chambers of Congress, allowing Trump to pursue his legislative agenda with support from his party.If Democrats take control of the House, they could block Republican-backed legislation and launch investigations into the administration. A Democratic-controlled Senate would also affect Trump's ability to secure confirmation for senior government and judicial appointments.However, prediction-market figures are not opinion polls. They reflect the prices at which traders buy and sell contracts on election outcomes, and can change as new information emerges. The final decision rests with the voters who will cast their ballots on November 3.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Jharkhand moves to set up PMU for eco-tourism projects
articles.summary: Jharkhand Eco Tourism Authority issues RFP to appoint a PMU to plan and implement forest eco-tourism via PPPs, sustainability studies, and community input.
articles.body: Ranchi: State govt has begun groundwork for a major eco-tourism push, with the Jharkhand Eco Tourism Authority (JETA) on Tuesday floating a request for proposal (RFP) to appoint a project management unit (PMU) for planning, investment and implementation of tourism projects in forest areas.The move is aimed at tapping the state’s tourism potential linked to its forests, wildlife habitats, waterfalls and tribal cultural heritage, while ensuring environmental sustainability and community participation.A key part of the proposed framework is mobilising private investment. An official said the PMU would help design public-private partnership (PPP) models, support procurement processes and engage with prospective investors for tourism infrastructure and services.The official said the initiative was part of the state’s shift from isolated tourism projects to an integrated and professionally managed eco-tourism ecosystem.According to the RFP, the PMU will function as JETA’s technical and strategic support arm. It will help identify potential eco-tourism destinations, prepare master plans, develop tourism products and create a pipeline of investment-ready projects.The agency will also assist in conducting carrying-capacity studies, environmental assessments and infrastructure gap analyses to ensure tourism growth does not adversely affect ecologically sensitive areas.Stakeholder consultations with local communities and government departments will form a key part of the exercise.“Besides destination planning, the selected consultant will assist in branding and marketing Jharkhand’s eco-tourism offerings, identifying funding sources and building local capacity through training and awareness programmes,” the RFP document stated.The PMU is proposed for an initial period of three years, extendable by another year based on performance.A multidisciplinary team comprising tourism experts, architects, engineers, procurement specialists and district-level consultants will support implementation, the document added.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. articles.title: Thota Tharrani Celebrates 60 Years in Art With Retrospective Exhibition
articles.summary: Thota Tharrani marks 60 years in art with a 1969–present retrospective at Lalit Kala Akademi, featuring 280 works and insights on process, cinema and AI.
articles.body: At the centre of the Lalit Kala Akademi gallery sits a large sculpture of a metal head with golden jaguars leaping out of it. “Have you heard the song ‘Always on my mind’? That’s what I call this one,” says its 76-year-old creator, artist Thota Tharrani. “I’ve always wanted to own a Jaguar. Never could afford the car. So, it’s always on my mind. Simple.”Tharrani is a straight shooter. What he sees is always what you get. Nothing more, nothing less in every one of his paintings in ‘Thota Tharrani: A Retrospective — 1969 to Present’, an exhibition which is on at the gallery till the end of the month, his 135th show to date, celebrating 60 years in art.“That’s Forces,” he says, pointing to a large canvas of thick dark swirls of acrylic. “I was in Delhi in 1978 when a freak tornado hit. That was what the world looked like to me at the time. So I painted it as I saw it. Until that year, I did only figurative art. The tornado made me try my hand at abstracts,” he says. “And that’s Sivaji over there,” he informs in the same monotone, pointing to the far end of the room.Wait, what, where, you wonder as you look around for a portrait of either the Tamil actor or the Maratha ruler. Instead, you find the painting of a feisty rooster.“Sivaji was my rooster,” says Tharrani with a rather nostalgic look in his eye. “I grew up with roosters, and had names for all of them. Unfortunately, my mother cooked one of them one day. I was upset because I felt she had cut up my creation and I refused to eat it.” But then he admits sheepishly that the sulking didn’t last long. “You see, my mother was a terrific cook.”That sense of attachment is why he often refuses to sell his work piecemeal. “I prefer to sell my collections as a whole. That way, I don’t feel like I’m losing something. On some days, I sit in the midst of my paintings in my garage. I don’t mind at all that they haven’t been sold.”Excerpts from an interview: Rajasthan, Ganeshas, Varanasi, forces of nature, Christ, scripts, Morocco … over the years, you have had so many muses. The 280 works on display at this show are not even a fraction of the number of paintings you have done over six decades.I have found inspiration in so many subjects that even I struggle to recall how many. Music for instance, has been a muse. There is a series I have done called ‘Symphony’, inspired by composers such as Vivaldi and Beethoven. When I heard it, I found that amidst the layers of bass, there is the sound of a violin that runs sharp and clear through the piece. That was the inspiration behind my distinct, sharp yellow lines amid the dark abstract base.One of my earliest muses was the junk in my house. I pencil-sketched everything I saw around me, a broken chair, leftover thatch, cracked vessels, anything piled outside my house. I made more than 40 drawings until my mother asked me, “At one time you told me to throw away all this junk. Now you’re sketching them!”Then one day, years later, a woman came asking for work for a children’s charity, and I gave most of my sketches away. I have only three of those original pieces left. Those drawings were the only memories I had of that house. Now I have very little left to remind me of how we lived. Do you finish one series before beginning another?I see it like the menu at home. On Monday, you eat something, then something else on Wednesday and Friday, then work your way back to Monday’s dishes. There is no fixed order. It’s the same with my muses. If you look at my work in periods of five or ten years, you will find the same subjects running through them.I might be painting Rajasthan in watercolour and suddenly switch to something else. After one or two paintings, I might change again. I have half a dozen subjects that I return to, and each series has at least 40 paintings. If I start painting something, I don’t stop until it is done.(Tharrani studied art at the Govt College of Fine Arts in Chennai. He studied printmaking in Paris in the 1970s, where he created more than 1,400 spot drawings on the city) So much so that you postpone everything else?I haven’t cut my beard and hair in years. I said I would shave it off at Tirupati, but I’ve been painting so much that I keep postponing the trip. So the hair and beard have been growing and growing. Now, no one will recognise me if I shave. It looks like this will be my look for a long time. What is your medium of choice?Easy. Whatever I can afford at that point in time. When it was only pencils, I did pencil sketches. Then came the more expensive watercolours and acrylics. You also make wooden sculptures.Yes, but I do not sculpt in wood. I collect pieces of scrap wood and put them together until a shape forms. That’s how I got the Hanuman sculpture. I work with whatever is discarded. Cinema has brought you National Awards (as art director for ‘Nayakan’ in 1987), the Padma Shri in 2001 and, in 2025, France’s Chevalier de l’Ordre des Arts et des Lettres. Which do you prefer, cinema or painting?I never really liked art direction. It was something I had to do for the money, and because my father was an art director. But cinema also helped me move between subjects. I would go away, work on a film, but always return to my paintings, which is what I love. Despite AI and computer-generated imagery, you still insist on drawing by hand.Nothing can replace what the human mind can do. That is creativity. I still sketch by hand. For me, it is better than anything AI can do. Why have you restricted photography at the exhibition?People have copied my paintings before. But I believe art is like a good curry. People may copy the recipe and change the garnish, but it won’t live up to the original. Still, I am not going to make it easy for them by allowing photography.(The Thota Tharrani retrospective has been curated by ArtWorld — Sarala’s Art International)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chennai | Silver Rate in Chennai | Bank Holidays in Chennai | Public Holidays in Chennai | Chennai AQI | Weather in Chennai | Petrol Price in Chennai | Diesel Price in Chennai | CNG Price in Chennai | LPG Price in ChennaiStay updated with the latest Chennai news. articles.title: A Georgia businessman promised investors 8% to 18% returns from small-business loans but diverted funds to luxury spending and politics; he has been sentenced to 15 years over a $76 million Ponzi scheme
articles.summary: A Georgia businessman who used religion and conservative politics to attract investors into a major investment fraud has been sentenced to 15 years in
articles.body: A Georgia businessman who used religion and conservative politics to attract investors into a major investment fraud has been sentenced to 15 years in federal prison. Chief US District Judge Leigh Martin May sentenced Edwin Brant Frost IV for running a $76 million (£58.5 million) Ponzi scheme that caused serious financial losses for more than 300 victims. Frost, 69, ran the fraudulent business through a company based in Newnan called First Liberty Building and Loan, LLC. The court also ordered him to pay $76,454,374.39 in restitution after he pleaded guilty to wire fraud charges earlier this year.Promises of high returns and community faithAccording to the United States Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Georgia, Frost promoted First Liberty as a lender that shared Christian values, supported conservative politics, and helped American small businesses. From around 2021 through July 2025, Frost asked individual investors to provide money for short-term "bridge loans" intended for commercial borrowers. He told investors their money was protected and promised monthly returns of between 8 percent and 18 percent. In marketing materials and presentations, Frost claimed First Liberty made money only from transaction fees and the difference between interest rates. He also told clients that borrowers would reliably repay the loan principal and interest through refinancing. He often claimed that borrowers had already received pre-approval for loans backed by the Small Business Administration. Federal prosecutors later revealed that these claims were almost entirely false. Few, if any, borrowers had received Small Business Administration pre-approval. By 2021, the company's legitimate lending business was struggling as several bridge loans failed to be repaid.Siphoning funds for luxury living and political influenceInstead of telling investors that loans were failing and the business was losing income, Frost hid the company's financial problems. He began using money from new investors to pay the interest owed to earlier investors, a practice known as a Ponzi scheme. Federal investigators found that Frost transferred at least $5 million of investor money directly into his personal accounts and related businesses. According to court documents made public by the Department of Justice, Frost used the stolen money to support an expensive lifestyle and increase his political influence. His personal spending included:$230,000 for a stay at a luxury holiday rental home in Maine.More than $140,000 spent at high-end jewellery stores.$20,800 for a luxury Patek Philippe watch.More than $335,000 paid directly to a rare coin dealer.More than $2 million used to pay his personal credit card bills.More than $570,000 directed towards political contributions.Federal prosecutors condemn exploitation of retireesThe collapse of First Liberty wiped out the life savings of hundreds of investors, including many retirees and older people who trusted Frost because of his religious beliefs and political views. Speaking about the case, US Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg strongly criticised Frost's actions and the misleading promises he made to investors."Like a false prophet and ravenous wolf in sheep's clothing, Frost used religion, politics, and promises of profitable returns to lure investors into giving him their hard-earned money. He wickedly exploited their faith to plunder their accounts and enrich himself," U.S. Attorney Hertzberg said in an official statement released by his office. "This was a stunning, sinful, and sacrilegious abuse of trust that wrecked hundreds of investors, including retirees and seniors who lost their life savings."Law enforcement officials also stressed the serious harm suffered by families who had trusted Frost with their financial security."Edwin Frost orchestrated a $76 million Ponzi scheme that devastated hundreds of investors who trusted him with their hard-earned money and financial futures. He exploited that trust to enrich himself, diverting millions for personal luxuries and political contributions while concealing the truth about his failing business," said Marlo Graham, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation's Atlanta Field Office. "Today's sentence holds Frost accountable for this massive fraud and reflects the FBI's commitment to investigating complex financial crimes and pursuing justice for victims."Inter-agency cooperation seals convictionThe complex financial investigation involved several federal and state agencies working together to trace where the diverted money had gone. Kyle A. Myles, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation Office of Inspector General (FDIC OIG) Atlanta Region, highlighted the importance of cooperation between law enforcement agencies in bringing major fraud offenders to justice. "Mr. Frost orchestrated a multi-million dollar Ponzi scheme that defrauded hundreds of investors and used the proceeds from the fraud on lavish purchases for himself. Today's sentencing brings him to justice for his crimes," Special Agent in Charge Myles said. "The FDIC OIG will continue to work with our law enforcement partners to investigate and hold accountable fraudsters who deceive innocent victims out of their hard-earned savings." Assistant United States Attorney Angela Adams prosecuted the case. The FBI and the FDIC OIG conducted the joint investigation, with additional help from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and the Office of the Georgia Secretary of State. Frost pleaded guilty to wire fraud charges on 12 May 2026. After completing his 15-year prison sentence, he will serve three years of supervised release.You use AI every day. articles.title: Bolsonaro’s party recognizes Brazil election result. But he hasn’t conceded
articles.summary: Brazil’s Liberal Party, the party behind presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, on Monday recognized the election results leading to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s victory, even though the far-right leader has not conceded. Party president Valdemar Costa Neto said in a statement posted on the social platform X that the party recognizes the election results but…
articles.body:
Brazil’s Liberal Party, the party behind presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, on Monday recognized the election results leading to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s victory, even though the far-right leader has not conceded.

Party president Valdemar Costa Neto said in a statement posted on the social platform X that the party recognizes the election results but that there were “questions raised about the vote” that need clarification.

“We recognize the presidential result proclaimed by the electoral court, but believe that the questions raised need to be properly clarified through a balanced and democratic political debate,” Neto said.

Da Silva, commonly known as Lula, defeated Bolsonaro after the country’s electoral court announced that the president led by 4.4 million votes in the second round of voting.

Bolsonaro had called for the election results to be annulled after Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin permitted Bolsonaro’s and Lula’s requests to keep polls open amid issues with flooding and transportation, respectively. The Brazilian outlet Folha de S Paulo reported that allies urged Bolsonaro to drop his calls for the results to be annulled.

After Bolsonaro’s loss, Argentinian news outlet Infobae reported that he traveled from Brazil into the province of Misiones. Another Argentinian newspaper, La Nacion, reported that an aircraft used to transport Bolsonaro landed in Iguazu late Monday and was expected to leave early Tuesday before its flight was canceled.

But the press office of Argentinian President Javier Milei denied Infobae’s reporting in a text to Bloomberg News .

“Argentina’s Migrations Office has no record of any entry by Flavio Bolsonaro into the Argentine Republic,” the press office told the outlet.

Another government spokesperson said Tuesday that there had been no request for asylum in Argentina from Bolsonaro, Bloomberg reported.

Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered Bolsonaro to surrender his passports and barred him from leaving the country, The Guardian reported . The order comes after Bolsonaro’s brother, Eduardo, said his brother should leave Brazil if he lost to Lula. The order refers to a criminal case over Bolsonaro’s alleged involvement in a money-laundering scheme.

Bolsonaro acknowledged the order in an Instagram video on Monday, saying he went to meet with his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest in the capital of Brasília.

The former candidate said “Lula’s federal police were at his door and in the middle of the street, and I was served with an order to hand over my passports and I am also prohibited from leaving the country.”

Lula received praise from world leaders and U.S. Democratic lawmakers for his election win, with many saying Brazil’s voters chose democracy. But some allies to the Bolsonaro family, including President Trump, questioned the results .

“It looked terrible to me,” the president told reporters Monday night. “I didn’t take sides, but it looked like another rigged election, frankly. It was a terrible look for the world. Elections have to be indisputable, and it looked very bad to me.”

articles.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio issued a warning to Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado on Monday, without explicitly naming her after the exiled Nobel Peace Prize winner returned to her home country.

“You’re not going to street-protest your way into a democracy,” Rubio told reporters, according to Axios.

He also praised her return, saying it was based on “the U.S. supported reconciliation talks which has already seen hundreds of political prisoners freed and hundreds of political opposition figures return from exile.”

Machado vowed to run for president if elections are held next year, telling other opposition leaders in Panama that she will remain committed to Venezuela’s transition of power and to holding free and fair elections.

A White House source told the outlet that the Trump administration’s capture of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and subsequent historic oil deal with his interim successor, Delcy Rodríguez, mark “the top foreign policy achievement[s] of this administration, and if the progress we made gets undone and Machado is a spoiler, nobody wins.”

The administration has publicly backed ruling-party loyalist Rodríguez, with President Trump saying Machado lacks support among the South American nation’s population while the interim leader wants to “make Venezuela great again.”

But Rubio told reporters this week the country must have elections and that the White House will not allow the nation’s government to stall until Trump leaves office in January 2029. He added that Rodríguez would have to declare the presidency vacant, triggering an election to be held in six months.

The secretary of state said he will oversee Venezuela’s transition as long as he’s in his job.

“Best-case scenario, I’m in this job for two more years and two months,” Rubio told reporters, according to Axios. “So, I clearly intend to see this thing well in advance of the time I leave.”

The top U.S. diplomat noted that Caracas must “change the infrastructure of the elections … quickly under timelines that we’ve established,” warning further that anyone attempting to interfere with this process is “doing great harm to Venezuela.”

The Trump administration has looked to move Venezuela away from the left-wing regime installed by former President Hugo Chávez, a military leader who led an unsuccessful coup against the government. He was first elected in 1999 and served non-consecutively until his death in 2013, leaving an opening for his vice president, Maduro, to succeed him.

articles.body:
Israeli voters headed to the polls Tuesday for a closely watched election that is widely regarded as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his administration.

The election, which could endanger Netanyahu’s nearly 19 years leading the country, has seen record turnout. Voting closed at 10 p.m. local time, or 4 p.m. EDT.

Here’s what to know about this pivotal election:

Many consider this election as one of the most consequential in Israel’s history, coming as Netanyahu faces scrutiny over his administration’s response to Hamas’ Oct. 7, 2023, attack on an Israeli music festival, which killed around 1,200.

Since the group’s assault, the prime minister has headed an ongoing military offensive in Gaza. As of late September, according to Gaza’s Health Ministry, the Palestinian death toll of Israel’s war had reached 74,000.

The prime minister, who has led the country on-and-off for nearly 19 of the past 30 years, has faced rising discontent among Israelis for his job performance.

Netanyahu is facing several challenges from major opposition party leaders, including his former military chief of staff and a right-wing nationalist.

Voter participation in this election hit an over 50-year high Tuesday , with strong turnout from Israel’s largest Arab-majority towns, The Jerusalem Post, an Israeli newspaper, reported.

Over 74 percent of eligible voters had cast their ballots as of 8 p.m. local time, according to the country’s Central Elections Committee (CEC). This was 3.7 percentage points more than the total turnout in Israel’s 2022 election.

Netanyahu has accused Arab voters in the country of “trying to steal the election” in his efforts to boost voter participation among his supporters.

“We’re at war for our home,” he wrote in a Tuesday post to social platform X. “Muslim Brotherhood supporters are raiding the polling stations and stealing the elections. Go out and vote, recover it!!”

The prime minister’s political party, Likud, announced plans earlier this month to send religious Jewish observers to polling sites in Arab communities to “prevent fraud.”

Critics accused the party of attempting to intimidate Arab voters, who make up a fifth of the country’s population, from voting in this election.

Israel’s elections differ from ones in the U.S in that citizens vote by party, not by the individual candidate. The proportion of votes each party receives is tied to the number of seats they earn in the Knesset, Israel’s 120-member legislature.

Party leaders will then have up to 42 days to assemble a coalition of at least 61 of the Knesset’s members — a simple majority — to support a candidate for prime minister.

If this effort fails, as is currently predicted by polling, Israeli President Isaac Herzog can pass the mandate to another lawmaker to try to fulfill within 28 days. If this is also not successful, the country will hold another election.

articles.body:
Brazilian Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro has fled Brazil for the U.S. after losing the runoff presidential election, multiple outlets reported Tuesday.

The move comes after Brazil’s Supreme Court ordered Bolsonaro to surrender his passports related to alleged financial crimes, The Associated Press reported.

The State Department did not immediately return The Hill’s request for comment.

Bolsonaro, a right-wing presidential candidate and the son of former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro, lost the presidential election in an upset to incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, commonly known as Lula. After losing the election, Bolsonaro claimed that it was fraudulent, just as his father had in 2022 after losing to Lula.

The elder Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year prison sentence for attempting a post-election coup in 2022.

President Trump got involved Monday, calling the election “rigged.” The president did not endorse Bolsonaro, but supported his father in 2022.

“I didn’t take sides, but it looked like another rigged election, frankly,” Trump said.

Trump and Lula have battled it out in the past, namely after the president levied 50 percent tariffs on Brazil.

The tariffs were at least in part a response to the elder Bolsonaro’s prosecution, Trump said. Lula threatened retaliation and authored an opinion column in The New York Times calling the tariffs politically motivated .

Trump’s support for the elder Bolsonaro and the opposition to his prosecution came amid his own legal troubles related to his actions after the 2020 presidential election. Trump has repeatedly claimed the election was stolen without evidence.

articles.body:
President Trump renewed calls for Venezuela to be the 51st U.S. state after touting the barrels of oil coming from the South American country.

“It will become a prosperous country, and who knows? Maybe someday soon, it will become a prosperous 51st state,” Trump said of Venezuela. “That’s possible. Let’s make it the 51st state.”

He said that “instead of a president, we’ll have an election for a governor.”

The president called out oil tycoon Harold Hamm in the crowd.

“Now let’s make it, Harold, the 51st state. You like that? I do. I do,” Trump said.

Trump said earlier on Tuesday that Venezuela sent 1 million barrels of oil to the U.S. as a “gift.”

Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio will oversee the Venezuelan tanker’s arrival on Tuesday, the New York Post reported. The crude oil will be processed in Texas refineries, Trump said.

A State Department official said Rubio is traveling with Trump to Texas in his capacity as national security adviser not as secretary of state.

“He needs time with the President on all kinds of issues. The president will be on the go, so being on the plane with him gives him a chance to talk to him about these items,” the official said.

The president has made comments about Venezuela becoming a state before. Trump said earlier this year that he was “seriously considering” making the country a state and has made similar comments about Canada.

Venezuela ’s acting President Delcy Rodríguez told journalists back in May that Venezuela has no plans of becoming a U.S. state.

“We will continue to defend our integrity, our sovereignty, our independence, our history,” she said, according to The Associated Press.

Rodriguez assumed power in January after the U.S. military operation that ousted then-President Nicolás Maduro.
